programs.name: Feeding America Food Bank Network
programs.org: Feeding America (200 food banks, ~60,000 local pantries and meal programs)
programs.gradeRationale: Walk in during open hours and leave with free food — nationwide coverage, no eligibility test, no cost, no appointment. The only real friction is finding hours and getting there.
programs.oneLiner: Free groceries from a local food pantry, usually same day
programs.whatIs: Feeding America is a network of about 200 food banks that supply roughly 60,000 neighborhood food pantries and meal programs. You visit a pantry near you and take home free groceries — often fresh produce, bread, canned goods, dairy, and meat. Many people come back weekly or monthly for as long as they need to.
programs.whoArrives: Anyone whose food ran out before the money came in — a lost job, a big car repair, benefits that didn't stretch. Most visitors are working families, seniors on fixed incomes, and people hit by one bad month.
eligibility: Anyone who needs help affording food
No income test at most pantries
Some pantries serve specific zip codes — check yours
Kids, adults, seniors — everyone welcome
programs.openTo: No immigration status requirement and no SSN — pantries are private charities that serve everyone and don't verify status.
programs.cost: $0 — the food is free. If a 'pantry' charges membership or fees, walk away; that's not the real network.
howToApply: Enter your zip code at feedingamerica.org/find-your-local-foodbank
Call Hunger Free America's Hunger Hotline at 1-866-348-6479 (Spanish: 1-877-842-6273), Mon-Fri 8am-8pm ET, if you'd rather talk to a person
Check your food bank's website or call for nearby pantry days and hours
Show up during open hours — bring bags or a cart if you can
docsNeeded: Usually none
Some pantries ask your zip code or family size on a short form
A few ask for any photo ID — foreign IDs are fine

claimChecks.claim: Using a food pantry can hurt your immigration case.
claimChecks.explanation: Food banks are private charities, and charitable food is not considered in the public charge test. Pantries don't report visitors to immigration.

claimChecks.claim: You need an ID and proof of income to get food from a pantry.
claimChecks.explanation: Feeding America says anyone who needs help affording food can visit. Most pantries ask at most your zip code or a short form about family size — no pay stubs, no proof.

claimChecks.claim: Food banks are only for people who are homeless.
claimChecks.explanation: Most people served are housed — working families, seniors, and people between jobs. Needing help this month is the only qualification.

programs.name: SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program)
programs.org: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration; applications run by your state agency
programs.gradeRationale: SNAP is an entitlement — everyone who qualifies gets it, with mandatory funding. But there's an application, an interview, document proofs, and stricter 2026 work rules; approval takes up to 30 days (7 days if you're nearly out of money).
programs.oneLiner: Monthly grocery money on a debit-style EBT card
programs.whatIs: SNAP (food stamps) puts grocery money on an EBT card every month. You swipe it like a debit card at most grocery stores and many farmers markets. The amount depends on your income and family size, and benefits continue as long as you qualify.
programs.whoArrives: People stretching a paycheck that won't cover both rent and groceries — workers with cut hours, new parents, seniors on fixed incomes, folks between jobs.
eligibility: Gross income under about 130% of the poverty line (about $3,483/month for a family of 4 through Sept 2026)
Net income under the poverty line (about $2,680/month for a family of 4)
US citizens and eligible green card holders
Adults 18-64 must work or train 80 hours/month unless exempt (pregnant, disabled, or caring for a child under 14)
Easier rules and higher deductions for seniors and people with disabilities
programs.openTo: Citizens and most green card holders (usually after a 5-year wait), plus Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA citizens. A 2025 law ended eligibility for refugees and asylees as of November 2025 unless they get a green card. Parents without status can apply for their US-citizen kids — only household members applying for benefits need an SSN.
programs.cost: $0 to apply. The real application is always free through your state — skip ads and websites that charge to 'file your SNAP application' for you.
howToApply: Find your state's application at fna.usda.gov/snap/state-directory (every state has its own form)
Apply online, by mail, or at your local SNAP office
Complete a short interview, usually by phone
Send proof of identity, income, and housing costs
Get your EBT card by mail — within about 7 days if you qualify for expedited service
docsNeeded: Photo ID or other proof of identity
Proof of income (pay stubs, benefit letters)
Rent or mortgage and utility bills — these can raise your benefit
Immigration documents for household members who are applying
SSNs for applying members only — non-applicants don't have to give one

claimChecks.claim: SNAP is only for people without jobs.
claimChecks.explanation: Most SNAP households with a working-age adult are working. You can earn up to the gross income limit — about $3,483 a month for a family of four — and still qualify.

claimChecks.claim: Getting SNAP counts against you as a 'public charge' and can cost you a green card.
claimChecks.explanation: Under the public charge rule in effect in mid-2026, SNAP is not considered — only cash assistance and long-term institutional care count. A rule change was proposed in late 2025, so check for updates if you're worried.

claimChecks.claim: Veterans and homeless adults are automatically excused from SNAP work rules.
claimChecks.explanation: The 2025 budget law removed those automatic exemptions, and states began enforcing the change in early 2026. Adults 18-64 must now work or train 80 hours a month unless they qualify another way, such as disability or caring for a child under 14.

programs.name: WIC (Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children)
programs.org: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration; run by state and local WIC clinics
programs.gradeRationale: Clinics are everywhere, appointments come fast (often within days, in person or virtual), and benefits typically load the same day you're certified. The only hurdles are an appointment and a few documents.
programs.oneLiner: Healthy food, formula help, and nutrition support for young families
programs.whatIs: WIC helps pregnant women, new parents, and kids under 5 eat well. You get an eWIC card loaded monthly for specific healthy foods — milk, eggs, fruits and vegetables, baby formula, cereal — plus one-on-one nutrition advice and breastfeeding support. Help lasts from pregnancy until your child turns 5.
programs.whoArrives: Expecting moms worried about affording formula and healthy food, and parents, grandparents, or foster parents raising little ones on a tight budget.
eligibility: Pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding women
Babies and kids under 5 — any caregiver can apply for them
Income at or below 185% of the poverty line
Automatic income pass if you're on Medicaid, SNAP, or TANF
A quick health and nutrition screening at your first visit
programs.openTo: No SSN ever required. As of mid-2026, Idaho is the only state that checks immigration status — the other 49 states enroll families without asking. WIC is not counted in the public charge test.
programs.cost: $0 to apply, and the food benefits are free.
howToApply: Check eligibility and find your local WIC agency at fna.usda.gov/wic
Call your local WIC clinic to book an appointment — in person or virtual
Bring ID for each person enrolling, proof of address, and proof of income or your Medicaid/SNAP/TANF card
Meet with WIC staff for a short health screening
Get your eWIC card and start shopping at WIC-approved stores and farmers markets
docsNeeded: ID for each person enrolling (kids' birth certificates or health cards work)
Proof of address, like a recent bill
Proof of income, OR your Medicaid, SNAP, or TANF card
Bring the kids or the pregnant applicant to the first visit

claimChecks.claim: WIC is only for moms.
claimChecks.explanation: Dads, grandparents, foster parents — anyone raising a child under 5 — can apply for that child. USDA says so directly on the WIC site.

claimChecks.claim: You need a Social Security number or legal status to get WIC.
claimChecks.explanation: WIC does not ask for or verify SSNs, and as of mid-2026 every state except Idaho enrolls families without checking immigration status.

claimChecks.claim: Getting WIC will hurt your immigration case.
claimChecks.explanation: Under the public charge rule in effect in mid-2026, WIC is not considered when deciding green card applications. A rule change was proposed in late 2025, so check for updates if you're worried.

programs.name: Free and Reduced-Price School Meals (National School Lunch and Breakfast Programs)
programs.org: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration; run by local school districts
programs.gradeRationale: Nearly every public school participates, and at high-poverty CEP schools every student eats free with zero paperwork. Otherwise it's one short self-reported form — but it only feeds enrolled kids on school days.
programs.oneLiner: Free or cheap breakfast and lunch at school
programs.whatIs: Schools serve breakfast and lunch every school day, free or at reduced price for families with lower incomes. At thousands of high-poverty 'CEP' schools, every student eats free with no form at all. One short application covers all your kids for the whole school year.
programs.whoArrives: Parents juggling grocery bills who want their kids to get two solid meals on school days — including families who just moved, lost income mid-year, or are new to the country.
eligibility: Free meals: household income at or below 130% of the poverty line
Reduced-price meals: income up to 185% of the poverty line
Automatic if your family gets SNAP or TANF, or your child is in foster care, Head Start, or a homeless or migrant program
Everyone eats free at CEP schools — no form needed
programs.openTo: No immigration status requirement in practice — schools don't ask or check. No SSN needed: the form asks only for the last 4 digits of one adult's SSN, with a box to check if you don't have one.
programs.cost: $0 to apply. Reduced-price meals cost at most 30 cents for breakfast and 40 cents for lunch; the free tier is fully free.
howToApply: Ask your school's front office for a meal application, or apply on the district website
Skip the form entirely if your school is a CEP school — every student already eats free
Tell the school if you get SNAP or TANF — your kids qualify automatically
Apply any time during the school year, not just at the start
docsNeeded: None at CEP schools
One application per household: names, income, and last 4 digits of one adult's SSN (or check the 'no SSN' box)
No documents to attach — income is self-reported

claimChecks.claim: The school meal form can expose your family to immigration enforcement.
claimChecks.explanation: Schools don't check or verify immigration status, and school meals are not part of the public charge test. The form even includes a box to check if you have no SSN.

claimChecks.claim: Every student has to fill out a form to eat free.
claimChecks.explanation: At CEP schools, all enrolled students eat breakfast and lunch free automatically, with no household applications. Kids in SNAP or TANF households are certified without a form too.

claimChecks.claim: If you missed the start-of-year deadline, it's too late to apply.
claimChecks.explanation: There is no deadline — families can apply at any point in the school year, including right after a job loss.

sources.title: National School Lunch Program | USDA Food and Nutrition Administration
Community Eligibility Provision | USDA Food and Nutrition Administration

programs.name: SUN Bucks (Summer EBT)
programs.org: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration; run by participating states, Tribes, and territories
programs.gradeRationale: Automatic for most eligible kids with no real application barrier — but a dozen states still don't participate, it's one $120 payment per child, and cards can be slow to arrive. Great where it exists; check your state first.
programs.oneLiner: $120 per child for summer groceries
programs.whatIs: SUN Bucks gives families $120 in grocery money per school-age child while school is out for summer. It comes on an EBT-style card, usually mailed automatically in late spring. It's one payment per child per summer, and it expires 122 days after it's issued — so spend it.
programs.whoArrives: Families whose grocery bills jump in June because school breakfast and lunch stopped — usually the same families using free or reduced-price meals during the year.
eligibility: School-age kids in participating states (38 states plus DC in 2026; Iowa is new, Texas and Florida still opted out)
Automatic if the household gets SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR
Automatic if the child is approved for free or reduced-price school meals
Other kids can apply if household income is within free/reduced meal limits
programs.openTo: No SSN required, and SUN Bucks is not counted in the public charge test. Cards go out automatically based on school-meal and SNAP records, and state applications don't ask about immigration status — though federal rules for food programs shifted in 2025, so check your state's site if you're worried.
programs.cost: $0 — it's automatic for most kids. Ignore texts or calls asking for your card number or PIN 'to activate SUN Bucks' — those are scams.
howToApply: Check whether your state participates at fna.usda.gov/summer/sunbucks
Do nothing if your child gets SNAP or TANF or is approved for free/reduced-price meals — the card arrives automatically
Apply through your state's SUN Bucks site before its summer deadline if your child wasn't auto-enrolled (Washington's 2026 deadline is Sept 4, for example)
Spend the $120 within 122 days — expired benefits can't be replaced
docsNeeded: None if your child is enrolled automatically
If applying: child's name, date of birth, school, home address, and household income

claimChecks.claim: SUN Bucks is available in every state.
claimChecks.explanation: For summer 2026, 38 states plus DC and all 5 territories participate. Iowa joined this year, but 12 states — including Texas and Florida — still opt out.

claimChecks.claim: You always have to apply to get SUN Bucks.
claimChecks.explanation: Most kids are enrolled automatically through SNAP, TANF, or their free/reduced-price meal approval. Only families not already in those systems need to apply.

claimChecks.claim: Getting SUN Bucks can hurt your immigration status.
claimChecks.explanation: SUN Bucks is not considered in the public charge test, and no SSN is required. Eligibility comes through school-meal or SNAP records.

programs.name: Commodity Supplemental Food Program (Senior Food Box)
programs.org: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration; boxes distributed by local food banks and community agencies
programs.gradeRationale: The food is real, free, and monthly, and signup is easy where it operates — but Congress caps the number of slots, not every county has a distribution site, and some areas keep waitlists.
programs.oneLiner: Free monthly grocery box for seniors 60 and up
programs.whatIs: CSFP — most people know it as the 'senior food box' — gives adults 60 and older a free box of groceries every month: cheese, milk, juice, fruits and vegetables, grains, and protein. Local food banks and community groups hand out the boxes, and some deliver. It's one of the best-kept secrets in senior food aid.
programs.whoArrives: Seniors on Social Security whose check runs out before the month does, and adult children or caregivers picking up a box for an aging parent.
eligibility: Age 60 or older
Income at or below 130% of the poverty line (limits set by your state)
Live in an area with a CSFP distribution site — it doesn't operate everywhere
Some states also ask about nutritional risk
programs.openTo: No SSN needed, and CSFP is not counted in the public charge test. A 2025 federal notice restricted CSFP on paper to citizens and 'qualified' immigrants like green card holders — but the nonprofit food banks that hand out boxes aren't required to check papers, and enforcement rules are still pending. If status is a concern, ask your local food bank what they require.
programs.cost: $0 — the monthly box is free.
howToApply: Find your state's CSFP agency through fna.usda.gov/csfp
Call your local food bank and ask about the 'senior food box' or CSFP
Fill out the short application with proof of age and self-reported income
Pick up your box each month — ask if your site delivers to homebound seniors
docsNeeded: Proof of age — any document showing you're 60 or older
Proof of address
Income is usually self-declared; most states don't ask for pay stubs

claimChecks.claim: If you get SNAP, you can't get the senior food box too.
claimChecks.explanation: You can receive CSFP and SNAP at the same time. The box is meant to supplement other food help, not replace it.

claimChecks.claim: You have to be a citizen with a Social Security number to get the box.
claimChecks.explanation: No SSN is ever needed, and green card holders and other 'qualified' immigrants can get the box, not just citizens. But a 2025 federal notice ended CSFP's fully open-to-everyone status on paper — verification rules are still pending, so ask your local food bank.

claimChecks.claim: Any low-income adult can sign up for CSFP.
claimChecks.explanation: Since 2020, CSFP serves only adults 60 and older. Women and young children who once qualified are now served through WIC instead.

programs.name: Meals on Wheels
programs.org: Meals on Wheels America and its network of local community programs
programs.gradeRationale: A program exists in almost every community and signup is just a phone call — but Meals on Wheels America itself describes a national waitlist crisis and says it reaches only a fraction of seniors waiting for help. Start dates range from days to months; once you're on, delivery is steady.
programs.oneLiner: Hot meals delivered to homebound seniors
programs.whatIs: Local Meals on Wheels programs deliver ready-to-eat meals to older adults who can't easily shop or cook — usually a hot meal around lunchtime, several days a week. The driver also does a friendly safety check, which for many seniors is the only visit of the day. Many programs also offer group meals at senior centers.
programs.whoArrives: Homebound seniors recovering from a hospital stay, living with mobility problems, or recently widowed and no longer cooking — often signed up by a worried adult child or neighbor.
eligibility: Usually age 60 or older (exact rules vary by local program)
Trouble shopping for food or preparing meals — homebound, recovering, or disabled
Younger adults with disabilities are served by some programs
No income test — payment is based on ability to pay
programs.openTo: No immigration status requirement and no SSN — local programs care about age and need, not papers.
programs.cost: $0 to apply. Meals may be free, suggested-donation, or sliding scale depending on the local program — most won't turn a senior away over money, but ask up front.
howToApply: Enter your zip code at mealsonwheelsamerica.org/find-meals
Call the local program and ask about eligibility, cost, and any waitlist
Complete a short intake — often a phone call or brief home visit
Start deliveries, and ask about group dining sites at senior centers too
docsNeeded: None — signup is a phone call or short assessment
Program staff may do a brief home visit to confirm need

claimChecks.claim: Meals on Wheels is always free.
claimChecks.explanation: It depends on the local program: meals may be free, suggested-donation, or charged on a sliding scale based on income. Most programs won't refuse a senior who can't pay.

claimChecks.claim: You have to be low-income to qualify.
claimChecks.explanation: Eligibility is about age (usually 60+) and difficulty shopping or cooking, not income. What you contribute is adjusted to what you can afford.

claimChecks.claim: You can sign up anywhere and start meals right away.
claimChecks.explanation: Many local programs are at full capacity, and Meals on Wheels America says demand has created a national crisis of waitlists. Start dates vary a lot by community — ask about the wait when you call.

programs.name: 211 Helpline (Housing & Shelter Navigation)
programs.org: United Way Worldwide and 200+ local 211 agencies
programs.gradeRationale: One free call works almost anywhere in the US, 24/7, with no paperwork and no questions about who you are. The network made over 19 million connections in 2025, and 9.1 million of them were about housing, homelessness, and utility bills — its biggest topic.
programs.oneLiner: Free 24/7 call that finds shelter and rent help nearby
programs.whatIs: 211 is a free helpline that connects you to real local help: emergency shelter, rent and utility assistance, food, and more. A trained person listens to your situation and gives you names, numbers, and addresses of programs near you that are actually taking people. It is not a government hotline that decides anything about you — it just opens doors.
programs.whoArrives: People holding an eviction notice, sleeping in a car for the first time, or one paycheck away from losing the apartment. Also family members trying to find help for someone else.
eligibility: Everyone — there is no income test
Covers 99% of the US population, including rural areas
No appointment, no application, no ID
programs.openTo: Open to everyone. No immigration status questions, no SSN needed — calls are confidential and can be anonymous.
programs.cost: $0 — calls, texts, and chats are free. 211 never charges. Anyone selling '211 assistance lists' online is a scam.
howToApply: Dial 211 from any phone and tell them you need housing help
Visit 211.org and enter your zip code if the call doesn't connect in your area
Ask specifically for 'coordinated entry' if you are homeless tonight
Write down every program name and number they give you
Call back as often as you need — different specialists know different programs
docsNeeded: none

claimChecks.claim: Calling 211 can get you reported to immigration
claimChecks.explanation: 211 calls are confidential and can be anonymous. Operators don't ask about immigration status and don't report to any enforcement agency.

claimChecks.claim: 211 only works in big cities
claimChecks.explanation: More than 200 local 211 agencies reach 99% of the US population, including rural areas. If dialing 211 doesn't connect, 211.org finds your local number by zip code.

programs.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline (Safe Housing Pathway)
programs.org: National Domestic Violence Hotline
programs.gradeRationale: Answered 24/7 by phone, text, or chat, free and confidential, and advocates can search a nationwide directory of DV shelters and programs while you're on the line. No paperwork to talk to someone; shelter bed openings depend on local capacity.
programs.oneLiner: 24/7 call or text that finds safe shelter from abuse
programs.whatIs: A free, confidential hotline for anyone dealing with abuse at home. Advocates help you make a safety plan and connect you to local domestic violence shelters, legal help, and programs that offer financial aid (the hotline itself doesn't hand out money). DV shelters are usually free and their locations are kept secret to protect you.
programs.whoArrives: People who need to leave a dangerous partner tonight but have nowhere to go, and people quietly planning an exit weeks ahead. Friends and family calling on someone's behalf, too.
eligibility: Anyone experiencing abuse — physical, emotional, or financial
All genders, all ages, LGBTQ+ survivors included
Kids can come with you to most DV shelters
You do NOT need a police report
programs.openTo: Open to everyone. No immigration status requirement, no SSN, no ID needed to call or to enter most DV shelters. Calls can be anonymous.
programs.cost: $0 — the hotline and most DV shelters are completely free. Tip: call from a safe phone; the number can appear on phone bills.
howToApply: Call 1-800-799-7233 (SAFE) any time, day or night
Text START to 88788 or chat at thehotline.org if calling isn't safe
Tell the advocate you need shelter — they search openings near you
Ask for a safety plan even if you're not ready to leave yet
Use espanol.thehotline.org for help in Spanish
docsNeeded: none

claimChecks.claim: If I call the hotline, they'll send the police to my house
claimChecks.explanation: The hotline is confidential and does not contact police or anyone else without you asking. You control what happens next.

claimChecks.claim: Domestic violence shelters only take women
claimChecks.explanation: Some shelters are women-only, but many serve men, LGBTQ+ survivors, and parents with kids. Hotline advocates find one that fits your situation.

claimChecks.claim: You have to press charges against your abuser to get shelter
claimChecks.explanation: No police report or charges are required. Shelters help based on your need for safety, not your legal case.

sources.title: National Domestic Violence Hotline

programs.name: Coordinated Entry & Street Outreach (Continuum of Care)
programs.org: HUD-funded local Continuums of Care (CoCs)
programs.gradeRationale: Every part of the US has a CoC, and emergency shelter through it can happen the same day with zero documents. But quality and capacity vary a lot by community, and the wait for actual housing (not just a shelter bed) can stretch to months.
programs.oneLiner: Your area's front door to shelter and housing programs
programs.whatIs: Every US community has a HUD-funded network called a Continuum of Care that runs shelters, street outreach teams, and housing programs. 'Coordinated entry' is the single front door: one intake conversation puts you in line for everything your area offers, from a shelter bed tonight to longer-term housing. Street outreach workers also come to you if you're sleeping outside.
programs.whoArrives: People sleeping outside, in cars, or in shelters, and people about to be evicted with nowhere lined up. Also parents of adult kids on the street trying to find the local outreach team.
eligibility: Anyone experiencing homelessness or about to lose housing
Emergency shelter has no income test
Longer-term housing programs prioritize the most vulnerable first
programs.openTo: Emergency shelter and street outreach are open to everyone regardless of immigration status; no SSN needed. Some longer-term HUD housing programs have status rules — the intake worker will explain.
programs.cost: $0 — shelter, outreach, and coordinated entry are free. Never pay anyone to 'get you into' a shelter or housing list.
howToApply: Call 211 and ask for 'coordinated entry' or 'homeless services' in your county
Search hud.gov/findshelter for shelters, food, and clinics near you
Look up your local homeless assistance contact at hudexchange.info/homelessness-assistance/homeless-help/
Walk into any shelter or day center and ask for a coordinated entry assessment
If you're outside, ask any outreach worker — they can start your intake on the spot
docsNeeded: None for emergency shelter
An ID and Social Security card speed up housing placements later — case workers help you replace lost ones for free

claimChecks.claim: You need an ID to stay in a homeless shelter
claimChecks.explanation: Emergency shelters generally take people with no documents at all. ID matters later for housing programs, and case workers help you get replacements.

claimChecks.claim: Shelters report undocumented people to immigration
claimChecks.explanation: Emergency shelter is open to everyone regardless of status, and intake workers are not immigration agents. Some longer-term federal housing programs do have status rules, but a shelter bed does not.

programs.name: Housing Choice Voucher Program (Section 8)
programs.org: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, via local Public Housing Agencies
programs.gradeRationale: The help itself is life-changing — rent capped near 30% of your income, for as long as you qualify — but getting it is brutal: most waitlists are closed, openings are often lotteries, and waits of 2-10 years are normal. Apply anyway and treat it as a long game.
programs.oneLiner: A voucher that caps your rent near 30% of income
programs.whatIs: Section 8 vouchers pay the gap between what you can afford and the actual rent on a private apartment you choose. You typically pay about 30% of your adjusted income and the voucher covers the rest, month after month, for years. Over 2 million families use it — the catch is getting one.
programs.whoArrives: Working families, seniors, and people on disability who can cover some rent but are being crushed by market prices. Many apply while couch-surfing or after an eviction scare.
eligibility: Income generally below 50% of your area's median (many spots reserved for below 30%)
At least one member with US citizenship or eligible immigration status
Some criminal history restrictions (varies by agency)
Priority often given to veterans, seniors, people with disabilities, and the currently homeless
programs.openTo: At least one household member must be a US citizen or have eligible immigration status, and those members need SSNs. Mixed-status families can currently get prorated (partial) assistance — but a rule HUD proposed on February 20, 2026 would end that for new applicants. It was still only a proposal as of mid-2026, so check the current rule before applying.
programs.cost: $0 to apply — always. PHAs never charge application fees. Websites charging money to 'register for Section 8' are scams.
howToApply: Find your local Public Housing Agency at hud.gov/contactus/public-housing-contacts or call (800) 955-2232
Ask which waitlists are open — apply to every PHA you'd be willing to move near, not just one
Sign up for waitlist-opening alerts from each PHA (openings can last only days)
Keep your address and phone updated with every PHA — a missed letter can knock you off the list
Ask about preferences (veteran, disability, homeless) that move you up the line
docsNeeded: Photo ID
Birth certificates for household members
Social Security cards for eligible members
Proof of income (pay stubs, benefit letters)
Immigration documents for eligible non-citizen members

claimChecks.claim: Section 8 waitlists are always open — you can just apply anytime
claimChecks.explanation: Most waitlists are closed most of the time and open briefly, sometimes as a lottery. You have to watch for openings and apply fast, ideally at several agencies.

claimChecks.claim: One undocumented family member disqualifies the whole household
claimChecks.explanation: Under the current rule, mixed-status families get prorated assistance based on eligible members. A rule HUD proposed on February 20, 2026 would end that for new families and require status checks for everyone — it was not final as of mid-2026 (comments closed April 21, 2026), so check the current rule and consider talking to a housing or immigration attorney.

claimChecks.claim: With a voucher you pay no rent at all
claimChecks.explanation: You normally pay about 30% of your adjusted monthly income toward rent and utilities (it can go up to 40% when you first lease a pricier unit). The voucher pays the rest.

programs.whatIs: The Justice Department keeps a public list of about 2,600 'accredited representatives' — trained non-lawyers at nonprofit groups who are legally allowed to handle immigration cases for little or no money. Check the list before you pay anyone. With very narrow exceptions, someone who isn't a licensed attorney and isn't on this list can't legally represent you.
programs.whoArrives: People who were burned (or almost burned) by a notario, or who found a cheap helper and want to make sure that person is real before handing over money and documents.
eligibility: Anyone can view and download the rosters — public record
Recognized orgs must be nonprofits serving low-income immigrants
They may only charge small, nominal fees
Listed by state and city so you can find nearby help
programs.openTo: Everyone, any immigration status; no SSN or ID needed to use the list
programs.cost: $0 to use the roster. Recognized orgs charge nothing or small nominal fees. Anyone charging thousands who isn't an attorney or on this list is likely breaking the law.
howToApply: Go to justice.gov/eoir/recognition-accreditation-roster-reports
Open the 'Organizations and Representatives, Listed by State' file
Find orgs in your city and write down their phone numbers
Call and ask for an intake appointment and their fee list
Cross-check any helper someone recommends against this same list
docsNeeded: None to use the list
For appointments: your immigration paperwork and any court notices

claimChecks.claim: Only lawyers can legally represent you in immigration matters
claimChecks.explanation: DOJ-accredited representatives at recognized nonprofits can legally prepare applications and, at the full level, even represent you in immigration court — often for a fraction of attorney prices.

claimChecks.claim: If you're in immigration court, the government gives you a free lawyer
claimChecks.explanation: Unlike criminal court, there is no public defender in immigration court — not even for children. You must find your own lawyer or accredited rep, which is why these free rosters matter so much.

programs.name: USCIS Fee Waiver (Form I-912)
programs.org: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)
programs.gradeRationale: Real money saved (hundreds of dollars per form) and free to request, but it takes paperwork, forces you to file on paper, and Congress made several newer fees un-waivable. A June 2026 proposal to end waivers for citizenship applications is pending, so the window may narrow.
programs.oneLiner: Ask USCIS to drop your application fee to $0
programs.whatIs: If you can't afford a USCIS filing fee, Form I-912 asks them to waive it completely — free to file. It can erase fees like the $760 citizenship application fee. You qualify if you get a means-tested benefit (like SNAP or Medicaid), your household income is at or below 150% of the poverty line, or you're in a sudden financial crisis.
programs.whoArrives: Green card holders who qualify for citizenship but can't spare $760, and low-income families renewing green cards or filing other waiver-eligible forms.
eligibility: You receive a means-tested benefit (SNAP, Medicaid, TANF, SSI), OR
Household income at or below 150% of Federal Poverty Guidelines, OR
Recent financial hardship (medical bills, job loss, eviction)
Your form must be on the fee-waiver-eligible list (N-400 citizenship, I-90 green card renewal, and others — check the I-912 instructions)
Good news for survivors: since April 2024, VAWA, T, and U visa filings have NO fee at all — no waiver needed
programs.openTo: No SSN required to request a waiver; open to anyone filing a waiver-eligible form, whatever their status. Survivors filing VAWA/T/U applications don't need this — those forms are already free.
programs.cost: $0 — the waiver request itself is always free. Never pay anyone who claims they can 'buy' you a fee waiver.
howToApply: Download Form I-912 (edition 07/22/25) at uscis.gov/i-912
Check the form instructions to confirm your application is waiver-eligible
Gather proof: benefit award letter, tax return, or pay stubs
Mail the I-912 in the same envelope as your application — you must file on paper, not online
Get free filing help from a DOJ-recognized nonprofit if the form feels confusing
docsNeeded: Benefit award letter (SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, TANF), or
Most recent federal tax return or pay stubs
Proof of hardship (medical bills, layoff notice) if claiming hardship

claimChecks.claim: It costs money to ask for a fee waiver
claimChecks.explanation: Form I-912 has no filing fee. You mail it with your application and, if approved, you pay $0 for that application.

claimChecks.claim: If you're low-income, any immigration fee can be waived
claimChecks.explanation: Fees created by the 2025 H.R.1 law — like the $100 asylum fee, the annual asylum fee, and the $500 TPS fee — cannot be waived by law, and DACA fees have never been waivable. Waivers still work for forms like the N-400 and I-90.

claimChecks.claim: Getting SNAP or Medicaid qualifies you for a fee waiver
claimChecks.explanation: Receiving any means-tested benefit is by itself a qualifying basis — you just need your award letter as proof and a waiver-eligible form.

programs.name: CLINIC Affiliate Network (low-cost immigration legal help)
programs.org: Catholic Legal Immigration Network, Inc. (CLINIC)
programs.gradeRationale: Over 420 affiliate offices in 49 states plus D.C. — the biggest network of authorized, low-cost immigration legal helpers in the country, and easy to find through one directory. Not an S because popular offices book up and waits vary by city.
programs.oneLiner: 420+ trusted low-cost immigration legal offices, one directory
programs.whatIs: CLINIC is the country's largest network of nonprofit immigration legal programs — more than 420 affiliate offices in 49 states and D.C. Every affiliate uses licensed attorneys or DOJ-accredited representatives, so the help is real and authorized. Most charge nothing or small flat fees far below private lawyers.
programs.whoArrives: Families handling green card petitions, DACA renewals, TPS, or citizenship who can't afford $3,000+ private attorney fees and want someone trustworthy in their own town.
eligibility: Anyone can use the directory to find an affiliate
Affiliates focus on low-income immigrants and their families
You do NOT need to be Catholic — services are for everyone
Each affiliate sets its own case types and fee scale
programs.openTo: Everyone, any immigration status — affiliates routinely help undocumented people; no SSN needed
programs.cost: $0 to search; affiliates are free or charge small flat fees — often a few hundred dollars or less per application vs. thousands at a private firm. Ask for the fee list before your appointment.
howToApply: Go to cliniclegal.org/find-legal-help and open the affiliate directory
Filter by your state or city
Call the nearest affiliates and ask about your case type, fees, and wait time
Book an intake appointment (some run walk-in workshops)
Bring all your immigration papers to the first meeting
docsNeeded: Photo ID if you have one (not required everywhere)
Any immigration documents: passport, receipts, prior applications, court notices
Proof of income if asking for free or sliding-scale service

claimChecks.claim: CLINIC affiliates only help Catholics
claimChecks.explanation: Affiliates serve people of every religion and no religion. The network is Catholic-founded but the services are open to all.

claimChecks.claim: Cheap nonprofit legal help means unqualified help
claimChecks.explanation: Every CLINIC affiliate provides representation through licensed attorneys or DOJ-accredited representatives — the same legal authority as a private firm, at a fraction of the price.

CLINIC Affiliate Directory

programs.name: RAICES Free Immigration Legal & Social Services
programs.org: RAICES (Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services)
programs.gradeRationale: Genuinely free, well-funded, and battle-tested — but it's Texas-only (five metro offices) and demand far outstrips staff, so intake can take weeks unless you're detained or facing an emergency. Outside Texas, use their model's cousins via ImmigrationLawHelp.org.
programs.oneLiner: Free immigration lawyers and case help across Texas
programs.whatIs: RAICES is a 40-year-old Texas nonprofit that gives free immigration legal services: deportation and asylum defense, help for detained families, DACA and TPS renewals, and family-based petitions. They also offer social services to help families get settled. Offices are in San Antonio, Austin, Corpus Christi, Dallas-Fort Worth, and Houston.
programs.whoArrives: Texans with a detained spouse or parent, asylum seekers with a court date coming fast, and DACA/TPS holders who need a renewal done right but can't pay a private lawyer.
eligibility: Live in Texas or have a case/detention there
Priority for detained people, families, and those in removal proceedings
Low-income focus, but no rigid income cutoff for intake
Case acceptance depends on capacity and case strength
programs.openTo: Everyone, any immigration status — including undocumented people and those in detention; no SSN needed
programs.cost: $0 — legal services are listed at no cost. If someone claiming to 'work with RAICES' asks you for money, it's a scam.
howToApply: Or use the contact form at raicestexas.org
Say clearly if someone is detained or has a court date — that speeds triage
Complete the intake screening they schedule
Gather your documents while you wait for case acceptance
docsNeeded: Any immigration paperwork: A-number, court notices, prior applications
ID or passport if available (not required)
Detention facility name and location if a family member is detained

claimChecks.claim: Applying for asylum is free
claimChecks.explanation: Under the 2025 H.R.1 law, filing the asylum application costs $100, plus an annual fee (currently $102, inflation-adjusted) for each year it stays pending — and these cannot be waived. Courts are reviewing the annual fee, but as of July 2026 it is being collected. The legal help at RAICES is still free.

claimChecks.claim: Contacting a legal aid group will get you reported to ICE
claimChecks.explanation: Nonprofit legal providers owe you confidentiality — what you tell them is protected, and their whole mission is defending you, not reporting you.

sources.title: RAICES — Home
RAICES — Services

programs.name: Citizenshipworks
programs.org: Immigration Advocates Network / Pro Bono Net (with the Immigrant Legal Resource Center)
programs.gradeRationale: A hidden gem: start your citizenship application tonight, for free, from your phone, with a real legal review available remotely — no office visit needed. It's an A because you still have the USCIS fee and processing timeline on the other side.
programs.oneLiner: Free online tool that walks you through citizenship, step-by-step
programs.whatIs: Citizenshipworks is a free website that guides you through the citizenship application (Form N-400) question by question, in plain language. It flags problems that could sink your case — like trips abroad or old arrests — before you file. It can also connect you to a nonprofit legal reviewer by video or find a free citizenship workshop near you.
programs.whoArrives: Green card holders who've been eligible for years but keep putting it off because the 20-page form feels scary, lawyer quotes are high, and they're not sure their record is clean enough.
eligibility: Green card holder for 5 years (or 3 years if married to a U.S. citizen)
Age 18 or older
Basic English (exemptions exist for age/long residence)
Passes the tool's free eligibility screening first
programs.openTo: For lawful permanent residents (green card holders) applying for citizenship — you'll have an SSN as an LPR; not for people without a green card
programs.cost: $0 for the tool and legal review help. The separate USCIS filing fee is $760 on paper / $710 online — but a fee waiver ($0) or reduced fee ($380) can apply if your income is low. Avoid paid form-filler websites that mimic this free service.
howToApply: Create a free account at citizenshipworks.org
Take the eligibility screening quiz
Answer the guided questions to build your N-400
Connect with a nonprofit legal partner for free remote review
File with USCIS — adding Form I-912 if you qualify for a fee waiver
docsNeeded: Green card (Permanent Resident Card)
Travel history for the last 5 years
Addresses and jobs for the last 5 years
Marriage/divorce records and kids' info if applicable
Court records for any arrest, even dismissed ones

claimChecks.claim: Applying for citizenship always costs $760
claimChecks.explanation: The standard fee is $760 on paper ($710 online), but if your income is at or below 150% of the poverty line (or you get SNAP/Medicaid) it can be $0 with a fee waiver, and under 400% it can be $380. Note: a June 2026 USCIS proposal would raise the fee and end these discounts — it is not final, so they still work today.

claimChecks.claim: You need to hire a lawyer to become a citizen
claimChecks.explanation: Most people with straightforward cases file successfully without a paid lawyer — free tools like Citizenshipworks plus a nonprofit review catch the issues that actually need a professional.

sources.title: Citizenshipworks
Apply for U.S. Citizenship with Citizenshipworks — LawHelpNY

programs.name: ILRC Red Cards (Know Your Rights Cards)
programs.org: Immigrant Legal Resource Center (ILRC)
programs.gradeRationale: Download, print, done — free in 59 languages, no signup, no status questions, usable the same minute you find it. The single lowest-barrier piece of immigration protection that exists.
programs.oneLiner: Free wallet card stating your rights if ICE shows up
programs.whatIs: Red Cards are small printable cards that state your constitutional rights — like staying silent and not opening your door — in plain words you can hand to an officer instead of speaking. They're free to download in 59 languages, from Spanish to Nahuatl to Yoruba. Millions are in circulation because they work for everyone, citizen or not.
programs.whoArrives: Mixed-status families making an emergency plan, parents worried about a workplace or home ICE visit, and teachers, churches, and clinics who want to protect their communities.
eligibility: Everyone — citizens, green card holders, undocumented people
No signup, account, or personal info needed
Immigrant-serving nonprofits and public defenders can request free printed batches
Anyone can print unlimited copies at home or a copy shop
programs.openTo: Everyone, any immigration status; no SSN, no ID, no registration — completely anonymous
programs.cost: $0 to download and print in all 59 languages. Only businesses, private attorneys, and very large orders (1,000+ cards) pay for printing via RedCardOrders.com. Never pay a website for a 'rights card' — the real one is free.
howToApply: Go to ilrc.org/redcards
Download the PDF in your language (59 available)
Print it, cut it out, and keep it in your wallet
Give copies to family members and make a family emergency plan
Request free printed batches through ILRC's order form if you're a nonprofit or public defender
docsNeeded: None

claimChecks.claim: You must open the door if ICE knocks
claimChecks.explanation: You do not have to open your door unless officers show a judicial warrant signed by a judge with your correct name and address. ICE's own administrative forms (like I-200/I-205) do not give them the right to enter your home.

claimChecks.claim: Undocumented people have no constitutional rights
claimChecks.explanation: The Constitution protects people, not just citizens. Everyone in the U.S. has the right to remain silent and to refuse consent to a search — which is exactly what the Red Card helps you exercise.

sources.title: ILRC — Red Cards / Tarjetas Rojas
Red Card Orders (ILRC's printing partner)

programs.name: Community Health Centers (HRSA Health Center Program)
programs.org: Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), U.S. Dept. of Health and Human Services
programs.gradeRationale: Health centers in every state saw 32.4 million patients in 2024, and federal rules require them to see you even if you can't pay a cent. Call or walk in — no insurance, no status questions, fees slide down to a few dollars.
programs.oneLiner: Doctor, dentist, and therapist visits priced by your income
programs.whatIs: These are nonprofit clinics funded by the federal government to care for everyone, insured or not. Visits are priced on a sliding scale based on your income and family size — often $20 to $40, sometimes less. Most offer medical, dental, mental health, and a low-cost pharmacy under one roof.
programs.whoArrives: People without insurance who have been putting off a checkup, a toothache, or a refill because of cost. Also new arrivals, people between jobs, and anyone whose regular doctor got too expensive.
eligibility: Everyone — no one is turned away for inability to pay
Sliding-fee discounts for incomes under 200% of the poverty line
No insurance required; they also take Medicaid, Medicare, and private plans
No immigration status questions
programs.openTo: No immigration status requirement and no SSN needed — health centers treat everyone and don't ask about status.
programs.cost: $0 to apply; visits cost a sliding fee based on income (often $20-40), and you're seen even if you can't pay
howToApply: Go to findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov and enter your ZIP code
Call the nearest center and ask for a new-patient visit on the sliding fee scale
Bring proof of income (a pay stub or tax form) so they can set your discount — you'll be seen even without it
Ask about dental, mental health, and pharmacy — most centers offer much more than checkups
docsNeeded: Photo ID if you have one (not required to be seen)
Proof of income (pay stub or tax form) for the sliding-fee discount
Insurance card, only if you have insurance

claimChecks.claim: You need health insurance to be seen at a community health center.
claimChecks.explanation: Health centers exist for the opposite reason — about 1 in 5 patients is uninsured. Fees slide with your income and no one is denied care for inability to pay.

claimChecks.claim: If you can't pay anything, they'll turn you away.
claimChecks.explanation: HRSA requires funded health centers to serve everyone, even people who cannot pay. The sliding scale can go to a nominal fee or zero.

claimChecks.claim: Going to a health center gets you reported to immigration.
claimChecks.explanation: Health centers don't ask about immigration status to treat you, and your health records are protected by federal privacy law (HIPAA).

programs.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
programs.org: SAMHSA (administered by Vibrant Emotional Health)
programs.gradeRationale: One three-digit number, free, staffed 24/7/365 nationwide, with no questions about who you are. Help starts the moment a counselor answers — usually within a minute or two.
programs.oneLiner: Free 24/7 crisis counselor by call, text, or chat
programs.whatIs: Call, text, or chat 988 from anywhere in the U.S. and a trained crisis counselor answers — free, any hour, every day. They listen, help you get through the moment, and connect you to local support if you want it. Spanish is available, and veterans can press 1 for the Veterans Crisis Line.
programs.whoArrives: People in a dark moment at 2 a.m. — and worried friends, parents, and partners who don't know what to say or do next. You don't have to be suicidal to call.
eligibility: Anyone in emotional distress or a suicidal crisis
Friends and family worried about someone else
Any mental health or substance use struggle counts — no crisis 'threshold' to meet
programs.openTo: Open to anyone; no name, SSN, or immigration status asked — you can stay anonymous.
programs.cost: $0 — calls, texts, and chats are free
howToApply: Call or text 988 from any phone, any time
Chat online at 988lifeline.org if you'd rather type
Press 1 after calling if you're a veteran, or 2 for Spanish
Ask the counselor for local follow-up resources before you hang up
docsNeeded: none

claimChecks.claim: If you call 988, police automatically get sent to your house.
claimChecks.explanation: Fewer than 2% of 988 contacts involve emergency services at all, and more than half of those happen with the caller's consent. Counselors contact 911 without consent only when someone is in immediate danger.

claimChecks.claim: 988 can trace your exact location like 911 does.
claimChecks.explanation: 988 does not use geolocation to pinpoint callers; calls are routed by area code (and newer routing uses only your general area to pick a call center, not to find you).

claimChecks.claim: 988 still has the dedicated LGBTQ+ youth option (Press 3).
claimChecks.explanation: The federal government ended the Press 3 / text-PRIDE specialized service on July 17, 2025, when its funding ran out. Officials have discussed relaunching a specialized service, but as of mid-2026 it has not returned. All 988 counselors still serve everyone, and The Trevor Project runs its own free 24/7 line for LGBTQ+ youth at 1-866-488-7386.

sources.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (official site)
988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (SAMHSA)

programs.name: Medicaid & CHIP
programs.org: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services + your state Medicaid agency
programs.gradeRationale: Once you're in, coverage is excellent — but income limits and rules change at every state line, applications take weeks to process, and missing paperwork is the top reason people get denied.
programs.oneLiner: Free or very low-cost health insurance for lower incomes
programs.whatIs: Medicaid is free or very low-cost health insurance for people with lower incomes; CHIP covers kids in families that earn too much for Medicaid. Coverage includes doctors, hospitals, prescriptions, and usually dental for kids. You can apply any day of the year, and in many states it can even pay medical bills from up to 3 months back.
programs.whoArrives: Workers whose jobs don't offer insurance, parents of uninsured kids, pregnant people, and anyone who just lost job-based coverage and is scared of one bad ER bill.
eligibility: Adults under their state's income limit (roughly $1,800/month for one person in the 40+ expansion states)
Kids in families earning up to about 2-3 times the poverty line, through CHIP
Pregnant people, seniors, and people with disabilities have extra pathways
You must live in the state where you apply
programs.openTo: Requires citizenship or certain lawful immigration statuses — and a 2025 federal law removes several lawfully present groups (like refugees and asylees) starting October 2026. Emergency Medicaid covers anyone regardless of status, and parents can apply for eligible kids without giving their own status or SSN.
programs.cost: $0 to apply; coverage is free or has small copays depending on your state
howToApply: Apply any time of year at healthcare.gov or directly with your state agency (find it at medicaid.gov)
Call 1-877-543-7669 (InsureKidsNow) to start a kids' application by phone
Gather pay stubs and birth dates for everyone in your household before you start
Answer any follow-up mail fast — most denials are for missing paperwork, and you can always reapply or appeal
docsNeeded: Proof of income (pay stubs or tax return)
Birth dates for household members
SSNs or immigration papers only for the people actually applying
Proof of address

claimChecks.claim: You can only sign up during open enrollment.
claimChecks.explanation: Medicaid and CHIP enroll year-round — there is no open enrollment window. You can apply the day you need it, and in many states coverage can reach back up to 3 months.

claimChecks.claim: If you have a job, you can't get Medicaid.
claimChecks.explanation: Eligibility is based on income, not employment. Millions of working people qualify, especially in the 40+ states that expanded Medicaid.

claimChecks.claim: Getting Medicaid for my kids will ruin my green card case.
claimChecks.explanation: Under the current (2022) public charge rule, Medicaid doesn't count against you except long-term institutional care — and benefits your kids use never count against you. But a rule proposed in November 2025 could broaden what officers consider, so mixed-status families should check with a nonprofit immigration lawyer before big filings.

programs.name: Hospital Charity Care (Financial Assistance) — free help from Dollar For
programs.org: Nonprofit hospitals (required by IRS rule 501(r)); Dollar For (nonprofit that files applications for you)
programs.gradeRationale: Charity care is a legal requirement at every nonprofit hospital — more than half of U.S. hospitals — and the nonprofit Dollar For files the paperwork for you at no cost. You do have to apply, income cutoffs vary by hospital, and decisions take a few weeks.
programs.oneLiner: Get big hospital bills reduced or erased for free
programs.whatIs: Federal law makes every nonprofit hospital offer 'charity care' — free or discounted bills for lower-income patients. On average, households under about twice the poverty line get bills fully forgiven, and discounts often reach about three times the poverty line. The nonprofit Dollar For checks your eligibility in about a minute and files the hospital application for you, free. This is one of the best-kept secrets in American health care.
programs.whoArrives: People staring at a hospital bill for thousands of dollars they can't pay — often months after the ER visit, sometimes after the collections calls have already started.
eligibility: Patients at any nonprofit hospital (more than half of U.S. hospitals)
Free care commonly for incomes under about 200% of the poverty line; discounts often up to about 300%
Both insured and uninsured patients can qualify
Bills up to at least 240 days old — even bills already in collections
programs.openTo: No immigration status requirement; hospitals verify income, not status, and most applications don't require an SSN.
programs.cost: $0 — Dollar For is free and so is every hospital's own application; never pay a 'medical bill negotiator' a cut of your bill
howToApply: Take the 60-second eligibility check at dollarfor.org
Let Dollar For's team prepare and submit the hospital application for you — free
Or ask the hospital billing office for its 'financial assistance policy' yourself — every nonprofit hospital must have one and post it
Send proof of income (pay stubs or tax return) when asked
Apply even if the bill is old or in collections — you have at least 240 days from the first billing statement
docsNeeded: The hospital bill(s)
Proof of income (pay stubs, tax return, or benefits letter)
Household size information

claimChecks.claim: A hospital bill is final — nothing can be done once it's issued.
claimChecks.explanation: IRS rule 501(r) requires nonprofit hospitals to accept financial assistance applications for at least 240 days after the first bill. If you qualify, the bill gets reduced or erased — even if it already went to collections.

claimChecks.claim: Charity care is only for people with no insurance.
claimChecks.explanation: Insured patients can qualify too — charity care can wipe out the deductibles and copays your insurance left behind, depending on the hospital's policy.

claimChecks.claim: You have to hire a bill-negotiation company to get help.
claimChecks.explanation: Hospital financial-aid applications are free, and the nonprofit Dollar For files them for you at no charge. Companies that take a percentage of your savings are selling you something you can get free.

programs.name: NAMI HelpLine
programs.org: National Alliance on Mental Illness
programs.gradeRationale: A real, trained person answers free of charge by phone, text, chat, or email — but only weekdays 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. ET, and what you get is guidance and connections to care, not treatment itself.
programs.oneLiner: A trained listener who finds mental health resources for you
programs.whatIs: A free national helpline staffed by trained volunteers who have lived with mental illness themselves or in their families. They help you understand symptoms, find affordable treatment, locate support groups, and figure out next steps. Open Monday through Friday, 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. ET.
programs.whoArrives: People newly diagnosed and overwhelmed by the system, and family members trying to help a struggling loved one who don't know where to start.
eligibility: Anyone with questions about mental health — for themselves or someone else
Family members and caregivers
Teens and young adults (dedicated peer support option)
No diagnosis, referral, or insurance needed
programs.openTo: Open to anyone; anonymous — no immigration status or SSN questions.
programs.cost: $0 — the helpline is free (standard carrier text rates may apply)
howToApply: Call 1-800-950-6264 Monday-Friday, 10 a.m.-10 p.m. ET
Or text 'NAMI' to 62640, chat at nami.org/help, or email helpline@nami.org
Tell them what's going on — they'll point you to treatment options, support groups, and local NAMI programs
Ask about NAMI's free classes for families if you're supporting someone else
docsNeeded: none

claimChecks.claim: The NAMI HelpLine is a suicide crisis line.
claimChecks.explanation: It's an information and emotional-support line, not a crisis service, and it's closed nights, weekends, and federal holidays. In a crisis, call or text 988 instead — it's free and answers 24/7.

claimChecks.claim: NAMI only helps people who already have a diagnosis.
claimChecks.explanation: A huge share of callers are family members, friends, and caregivers. You can call about someone else's situation, or just to figure out whether what you're feeling needs care.
