programs.name: Free & Charitable Clinics (NAFC network)
programs.org: National Association of Free & Charitable Clinics (NAFC) and its member clinics
programs.gradeRationale: 1,400+ clinics and pharmacies see about 1.7 million patients a year with little or no paperwork and free or donation-based care — but coverage depends on where you live, and some clinics have limited hours or waitlists.
programs.oneLiner: Free medical care at 1,400+ volunteer-run clinics
programs.whatIs: A national network of more than 1,400 volunteer-run clinics and pharmacies that care for people who fall through the cracks of the health system. Care is free or a small suggested donation. Many offer medical, dental, vision, mental health, and help getting medications.
programs.whoArrives: Working people without insurance whose income is a bit too high for Medicaid in their state, or who need care right now while a Medicaid application is still pending.
eligibility: Typically uninsured or underinsured people
Income limits vary by clinic (often under 2-3 times the poverty line)
Each clinic sets its own rules — many ask for nothing beyond need
programs.openTo: Most clinics don't ask about immigration status or require an SSN, but each clinic sets its own rules — call ahead to confirm.
programs.cost: $0 to apply; care is free or a small voluntary donation at most clinics
howToApply: Search your ZIP code at nafcclinics.org/find-clinic
Call the clinic first — hours, services, and rules differ from place to place
Ask what to bring; many want proof of income or of being uninsured, some need nothing
Arrive early — some clinics see walk-ins first come, first served
docsNeeded: Varies by clinic — often proof of income and proof you're uninsured; some clinics ask for nothing

claimChecks.claim: Free clinics are only for homeless people.
claimChecks.explanation: Most patients are working people whose jobs don't offer insurance or whose income is just over their state's Medicaid line. The network serves about 1.7 million patients a year.

claimChecks.claim: You need an ID and a Social Security number to be seen.
claimChecks.explanation: Many free clinics require neither, but each one sets its own intake rules. A quick phone call tells you exactly what — if anything — to bring.

sources.title: Find a Clinic (NAFC)
About NAFC

programs.name: Prescription Patient Assistance Programs (via NeedyMeds & RxAssist)
programs.org: Drug manufacturers' assistance programs; navigated free through NeedyMeds (nonprofit) and RxAssist
programs.gradeRationale: The medicine is genuinely free and the programs are well funded, but every drug company has its own form, you need a doctor's signature, shipping takes weeks, and you have to reapply about once a year.
programs.oneLiner: Free brand-name prescriptions shipped straight from drug makers
programs.whatIs: Most brand-name drug makers run patient assistance programs (PAPs) that ship free medicine to people with low incomes and little or no drug coverage. The nonprofits NeedyMeds and RxAssist keep free directories of every program and its application form — this is the classic hidden-in-plain-sight lifeline. NeedyMeds also offers a free discount card that cuts up to 80% off many medicines at most U.S. pharmacies, with no sign-up.
programs.whoArrives: People rationing insulin, inhalers, or heart medicine because a brand-name drug costs hundreds of dollars a month — and seniors hitting gaps in their drug coverage.
eligibility: Income under each program's limit (commonly 2-4 times the poverty line)
Little or no prescription coverage for that specific drug
U.S. residency for most programs
A prescription from any licensed prescriber
programs.openTo: Most drug-company programs require U.S. residency but many don't ask for an SSN; NeedyMeds' directory, helpline, and discount card require nothing at all.
programs.cost: $0 to apply directly; beware websites charging 'processing fees' for the exact same free forms
howToApply: Look up each of your medicines at needymeds.org or rxassist.org
Or call the free NeedyMeds helpline at 1-800-503-6897 (weekdays 9-5 ET) and let them search for you
Print the drug company's application and have your doctor sign the prescriber section
Mail or fax it with proof of income; medicine usually ships to your home or doctor's office in 2-6 weeks
Reapply each year — most approvals last 12 months
docsNeeded: Doctor's signature on the program application
Proof of income (tax return or pay stubs)
Proof you lack drug coverage, for some programs

claimChecks.claim: Drug companies never give away brand-name medicine.
claimChecks.explanation: Most major manufacturers run patient assistance programs that ship free brand-name drugs to people who meet income rules — they've operated for decades and fill millions of prescriptions a year.

claimChecks.claim: You have to pay a service to apply for you.
claimChecks.explanation: Applying is always free. NeedyMeds and RxAssist post the same applications the paid middlemen use — never pay a 'fee' for a free form.

claimChecks.claim: If you have any insurance, you can't get help.
claimChecks.explanation: Some programs are uninsured-only, but many help people whose plan won't cover a drug or whose copays are unaffordable, and Medicare Part D patients often qualify. Check each drug's rules.

sources.title: NeedyMeds — Find help with the cost of medicine
RxAssist Patient Center

programs.name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)
programs.org: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, run by states, tribes, and territories
programs.gradeRationale: Every state runs it and applying is simple, but money is first-come, first-served and often runs out mid-season — you have to apply the day your state's window opens. Crisis help for shutoffs can move within about 48 hours, which saves the grade.
programs.oneLiner: Help paying heating and cooling bills, plus shutoff emergencies
programs.whatIs: LIHEAP is a federal program that helps pay home energy bills. Most people get a one-time grant paid straight to their utility company, often a few hundred dollars per season. Many states also offer fast crisis help if you have a shutoff notice, plus free furnace repairs and weatherization.
programs.whoArrives: People staring at a shutoff notice in January, seniors on fixed incomes when the summer AC bill spikes, and families whose paycheck can't stretch to cover both rent and the gas bill.
eligibility: Income at or below your state's limit (roughly 150% of the poverty line or 60% of state median income)
Renters and homeowners both qualify
Automatic eligibility in many states if you already get SNAP, SSI, or TANF
Priority often goes to households with seniors, young kids, or a person with a disability
programs.openTo: At least one household member must be a U.S. citizen or 'qualified' immigrant (green card, refugee, asylee, COFA citizen); mixed-status families can get pro-rated help in many states. States usually ask for SSNs of household members.
programs.cost: $0 to apply. Ignore any website charging an 'application fee' — those are scams; the official program never charges a fee, and the real application is always free through your state or local agency.
howToApply: Call the National Energy Assistance Referral hotline at 1-866-674-6327 (weekdays) to find your local LIHEAP office
Look up your state or tribal office on the official ACF contact list (acf.gov) or at EnergyHelp.us
Apply the first day your state's window opens — funds run out fast in many states
Bring your utility bill and proof of income; ask about crisis assistance if you have a shutoff notice
docsNeeded: Recent utility bill or shutoff notice
Photo ID
Proof of household income (pay stubs, benefit letters)
SSNs for household members (state rules vary)

claimChecks.claim: Renters can't get LIHEAP — it's only for homeowners.
claimChecks.explanation: Renters qualify. In many states you can even get help when heat is included in your rent.

claimChecks.claim: Getting LIHEAP can hurt your green card application.
claimChecks.explanation: LIHEAP is not cash assistance, so it does not count in the public charge test — under the rule in effect now, only cash aid like TANF or SSI counts. A rule change has been proposed, so if you're worried, check with a free immigration legal aid office for the latest.

claimChecks.claim: You can apply for LIHEAP any time of year.
claimChecks.explanation: Each state sets its own application windows (often fall and winter), and most stop taking applications when the money runs out. Apply early.

sources.title: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) — ACF
LIHEAP State and Territory Contact Listing — ACF

programs.name: Lifeline
programs.org: Federal Communications Commission / Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC)
programs.gradeRationale: National, funded by phone-bill fees rather than annual budgets, and the online eligibility check often approves you in minutes. You still have to pick a participating phone or internet company afterward, and the discount is modest.
programs.oneLiner: Monthly $9.25 discount on your phone or internet bill
programs.whatIs: Lifeline takes up to $9.25 a month off phone or internet service, and up to $34.25 on tribal lands. Some companies apply it so a basic plan costs you nothing. It keeps going month after month as long as you qualify and reconfirm once a year.
programs.whoArrives: People who lost the ACP internet discount when that program ended in 2024, job hunters who can't afford to lose their phone number, and anyone on SNAP or Medicaid trying to trim a monthly bill.
eligibility: Income at or below 135% of the federal poverty line, OR
You (or your child or dependent) get SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, federal public housing assistance, or the Veterans Pension
Survivors of domestic violence or trafficking can qualify at up to 200% of the poverty line, or through WIC, school meals, or a Pell Grant
One discount per household
Bigger benefit if you live on qualifying tribal lands
programs.openTo: No citizenship requirement, but the application asks for the last 4 digits of an SSN or a Tribal ID number — people with neither will hit a wall.
programs.cost: $0 to apply. Use only lifelinesupport.org or a real participating provider — ignore sites that charge a fee to 'sign you up.'
howToApply: Check if you qualify and apply at lifelinesupport.org (the official National Verifier)
Upload proof if the system can't confirm you automatically — a SNAP or Medicaid award letter works
Pick a participating phone or internet company once approved; the site lists companies near you
Recertify once a year when USAC contacts you so the discount doesn't stop
docsNeeded: Last 4 digits of your SSN or a Tribal ID number
Proof of program enrollment (like a SNAP letter) or proof of income, if not auto-verified
Photo ID if requested

claimChecks.claim: Lifeline is the 'Obama phone' program he created.
claimChecks.explanation: Lifeline started in 1985 under President Reagan. Free cell phone offers came later through participating companies — no president hands out phones.

claimChecks.claim: Lifeline ended when the ACP internet program ended.
claimChecks.explanation: The Affordable Connectivity Program ran out of money and stopped in mid-2024. Lifeline is a separate, older program that is still running today.

sources.title: Lifeline Support for Affordable Communications (official consumer site)
Lifeline Program — USAC

programs.name: VITA Free Tax Prep + Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
programs.org: Internal Revenue Service, delivered through community partner sites
programs.gradeRationale: Thousands of free sites nationwide every tax season with IRS-certified volunteers, and the payoff can be thousands of dollars in refundable credits. The catch: most sites only run January through April, and popular ones book up.
programs.oneLiner: Free tax filing that can unlock a refund worth thousands
programs.whatIs: IRS-certified volunteers prepare and file your taxes for free if you make about $69,000 or less. Filing is how you claim the Earned Income Tax Credit — worth up to $8,046 for a family with three or more kids on 2025 returns — plus the Child Tax Credit. Many low-wage workers are owed money and don't know it.
programs.whoArrives: Working parents who've been paying a tax-prep chain $300 to get at their own refund, gig workers confused by 1099s, and people who skipped filing for a few years and suspect the IRS owes them.
eligibility: Household income around $69,000 or less for VITA
People with disabilities and limited-English speakers can get help at many sites regardless of income
TCE sites (often run by AARP) focus on people 60 and older
For the EITC itself: you worked during the year and earned under the limit (up to $68,675 for married filers with 3+ kids on 2025 returns)
programs.openTo: VITA helps ITIN filers, and some sites even process ITIN applications — no immigration status is needed for the free tax prep itself. The federal EITC does require SSNs valid for work for you, your spouse, and your qualifying kids.
programs.cost: $0 — that's the whole point. If a 'free' site tries to charge you or push a refund-advance loan, walk out; real VITA sites never charge.
howToApply: Find a site with the IRS VITA/TCE locator (freetaxassistance.for.irs.gov/s/sitelocator) or call 800-906-9887
Book an appointment early in the season — January-to-April slots fill fast
Bring photo ID, Social Security or ITIN documents for everyone on the return, and your W-2s and 1099s
Ask the volunteer to check the past 3 years too — you can still claim refunds you missed
docsNeeded: Photo ID
Social Security cards or ITIN letters for everyone on the return
W-2s, 1099s, and other income forms
Bank account info for direct deposit (optional, but refunds arrive faster)

claimChecks.claim: You need kids to get the EITC.
claimChecks.explanation: Workers without kids can get it too — up to $649 on 2025 returns if you're roughly age 25-64 and earn under about $19,104 ($26,214 married).

claimChecks.claim: Claiming the EITC can count against you in a green card 'public charge' test.
claimChecks.explanation: Tax credits are not considered in the public charge test. Under the rule in effect now, only cash assistance like TANF or SSI counts.

claimChecks.claim: Volunteer tax preparers make mistakes — you get what you pay for.
claimChecks.explanation: VITA volunteers must pass IRS tax-law certification every year, and the IRS requires a second quality review of every return before it's filed.

sources.title: Free tax return preparation for qualifying taxpayers — IRS
Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — IRS

programs.name: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF)
programs.org: HHS Administration for Children & Families, run by states
programs.gradeRationale: It exists in every state, but monthly amounts are small, the paperwork and work requirements are heavy, and states approve far fewer families than apply. Expect an interview, a document chase, and a 30-45 day wait.
programs.oneLiner: Monthly cash for very-low-income families with children
programs.whatIs: TANF is monthly cash assistance for families with kids (and pregnant people) who have very little income. Amounts vary wildly by state — roughly $200 to $1,100 a month for a family of three. Most adults must do work or training activities, and federal aid has a 60-month lifetime limit.
programs.whoArrives: Single parents between jobs with nothing left after rent, grandparents suddenly raising grandkids, and parents leaving a violent home who need any cash floor at all.
eligibility: Families with a child under 18, or a pregnant person
Very low income and few assets — cutoffs vary a lot by state
Adults usually must accept work or job-training requirements
Grandparents and other relatives raising kids can apply for 'child-only' aid
programs.openTo: Adults generally need citizen or 'qualified' immigrant status, often with a 5-year wait after getting a green card. U.S.-citizen kids qualify even when their parents don't — parents can file a 'child-only' case. SSNs are requested for the people who will receive aid.
programs.cost: $0 to apply.
howToApply: Find your state's TANF office through the ACF 'Help for Families' page (acf.gov) or your state benefits portal
Apply online, by phone, or at your county human services office — many states bundle TANF with SNAP and Medicaid applications
Complete the required interview and turn in documents fast; missing paperwork is the top reason applications die
Ask about 'diversion' payments — some states offer one-time emergency cash instead of monthly aid
docsNeeded: Photo ID and kids' birth certificates
Proof of income and expenses (pay stubs, rent, utilities)
SSNs for the family members who will receive aid
Proof of address

claimChecks.claim: Getting TANF can count against you in a green card 'public charge' decision.
claimChecks.explanation: Cash assistance like TANF is one of the few benefits that does count under the rule in effect now — but only cash YOU receive, not benefits your kids get. Rules can change, so talk to a free immigration legal aid office before deciding.

claimChecks.claim: Undocumented parents can't get TANF for their U.S.-citizen kids.
claimChecks.explanation: Citizen kids qualify on their own. Parents can file a 'child-only' case where the aid is for the children — the parents themselves receive nothing.

claimChecks.claim: There's no time limit on cash welfare.
claimChecks.explanation: Federal law caps federally-funded TANF at 60 months in a lifetime for most adults, and some states set shorter limits.

sources.title: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) — ACF
Help for Families (find your state TANF office) — ACF

programs.name: Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
programs.org: Social Security Administration
programs.gradeRationale: The money is reliable once you're in — up to $994 a month in 2026 — but disability decisions commonly take many months and most first applications are denied. Seniors 65+ applying without a disability claim move much faster.
programs.oneLiner: Monthly cash if you're disabled, blind, or 65+ with little income
programs.whatIs: SSI pays monthly cash — up to $994 for one person and $1,491 for a couple in 2026 — to people who are 65 or older, blind, or disabled and have very little income and savings. Some states add extra money on top, and SSI usually comes with Medicaid automatically.
programs.whoArrives: People too sick to keep working who never earned enough for regular Social Security, parents of children with serious disabilities, and seniors whose retirement check is tiny or nonexistent.
eligibility: Age 65+, blind, or a disability expected to last 12+ months (children with disabilities count)
Very low income
Under $2,000 in countable assets ($3,000 for a couple) — your home and one car don't count
Live in the United States
programs.openTo: Requires U.S. citizenship or narrow 'qualified' immigrant categories (refugees and asylees in their first 7 years, certain green-card holders with 10 years of work credits, and a few others). SSN required.
programs.cost: $0 to apply. Never pay anyone up front to 'file for you' — legitimate disability lawyers only get paid a capped share of your back pay if you win.
howToApply: Start online at ssa.gov/ssi or call 1-800-772-1213 to set up an appointment
Gather medical records and a list of every doctor, clinic, and medication
Answer SSA's follow-up letters fast — missed deadlines sink claims
If denied, appeal within 60 days; many people win on appeal, and free legal aid can help
docsNeeded: Birth certificate or other proof of age
Medical records and doctors' contact info (for disability claims)
Bank statements and proof of income and assets
Proof of citizenship or qualified immigration status

claimChecks.claim: You need a work history to get SSI.
claimChecks.explanation: SSI has no work requirement at all — that's SSDI, a different program. SSI is based on need, not work credits.

claimChecks.claim: SSI and Social Security retirement are the same thing.
claimChecks.explanation: They're different programs. SSI is need-based cash for people who are 65+, blind, or disabled — you can get it even if you never paid into Social Security.

claimChecks.claim: Getting SSI can count against a green card application.
claimChecks.explanation: SSI is cash assistance, one of the few benefits counted in the public charge test. Most people who can even qualify for SSI already hold protected statuses, but check with an immigration attorney first.

sources.title: Supplemental Security Income (SSI) — SSA
How much you could get from SSI — SSA

programs.name: Unemployment Insurance (UI)
programs.org: U.S. Department of Labor, run by state workforce agencies
programs.gradeRationale: If you clearly lost a job through no fault of your own, checks usually start in 2-3 weeks. But state systems are clunky, disputed claims drag on for months, and benefit amounts differ hugely by state.
programs.oneLiner: Weekly cash after losing your job through no fault of yours
programs.whatIs: UI replaces part of your paycheck — often 40-50%, with a state cap — while you look for a new job. Most states pay for up to 26 weeks. You file with the state where you worked, then confirm every week or two that you're still job hunting.
programs.whoArrives: People laid off in a downsizing, seasonal workers between contracts, and folks whose hours were cut so deep they can't cover rent.
eligibility: Lost your job or major hours through no fault of your own — layoffs, closures, cut shifts
Earned enough wages in your state's 'base period' (roughly the past 12-18 months)
Able to work, available to work, and actively looking
Quitting for 'good cause' — unsafe conditions, and in many states fleeing domestic violence — can still qualify
programs.openTo: Requires an SSN and legal work authorization — both when the wages were earned and while you're claiming. Undocumented workers generally cannot collect UI even though their employers paid taxes on their wages.
programs.cost: $0 to file. Only use your state's official .gov site — lookalike sites that charge 'filing fees' are scams.
howToApply: File the same week you lose your job — most states won't backdate your claim
Find your state's official filing site through CareerOneStop's Unemployment Benefits Finder or call 1-877-872-5627
Have 18 months of work history ready: employer names, addresses, dates, and pay
Certify every week or two as instructed, even while your claim is still pending
Appeal fast if denied — deadlines are short and many denials get reversed
docsNeeded: SSN and photo ID
Employment history for the last 18 months (employers, dates, wages)
Alien registration number if you're not a citizen
Bank info for direct deposit

claimChecks.claim: If you quit your job, you can never get unemployment.
claimChecks.explanation: Quitting usually disqualifies you, but 'good cause' quits — unsafe conditions, medical necessity, and in many states escaping domestic violence — can still qualify. Apply anyway and let the state decide.

claimChecks.claim: Unemployment money was deducted from your old paychecks.
claimChecks.explanation: It's funded by taxes your employers paid, not deductions from your pay (except small worker contributions in Alaska, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania). You're claiming insurance you already earned, not charity.

sources.title: Unemployment Insurance — U.S. Department of Labor
Unemployment Benefits Finder — CareerOneStop

programs.name: National Diaper Bank Network (free diapers)
programs.org: National Diaper Bank Network and its 200+ local member diaper banks
programs.gradeRationale: Hundreds of member banks serve nearly 320,000 kids a month, and getting diapers is usually one 211 call plus a pickup — no forms, no waitlist. Not an S only because rural coverage has gaps and monthly quantities are limited.
programs.oneLiner: Free diapers for your baby through a local diaper bank
programs.whatIs: Diaper banks give out free diapers — usually a few dozen per child per month — through local pantries, churches, and family centers. NDBN is the national network behind more than 200 of them, serving nearly 320,000 children a month. Many also stock baby wipes, period supplies, and adult incontinence products.
programs.whoArrives: Parents choosing between diapers and groceries in the last week of the month, grandparents raising babies on a pension, and moms who learned the hard way that SNAP and WIC won't buy diapers.
eligibility: Have a baby or toddler in diapers (many banks also carry youth and adult sizes)
Low income — most banks don't do formal income checks
Live near a member bank or one of its partner agencies
Each local bank sets its own simple rules
programs.openTo: No immigration status requirement and no SSN — these are private charities, not government programs. Most banks just ask basic info like your zip code and your kids' ages.
programs.cost: $0 — diapers are free. If anyone charges you, it's not a real diaper bank.
howToApply: Dial 211 (or search 211.org) and ask for 'diapers' or 'basic needs' — NDBN's own advice for finding help near you
Check NDBN's member directory at nationaldiaperbanknetwork.org to find a bank near you
Call the local bank or its partner agency to learn distribution days — many hand out diapers through food pantries and family centers
If nothing turns up, try local food pantries and faith-based groups — many distribute diapers too
docsNeeded: Usually none
Some locations ask for a photo ID or your child's age and diaper size

claimChecks.claim: You can buy diapers with SNAP or WIC.
claimChecks.explanation: Neither program covers diapers — federal rules treat them like paper goods, not food. That gap is exactly what diaper banks exist to fill.

claimChecks.claim: Using a diaper bank can hurt your immigration case.
claimChecks.explanation: Diaper banks are private charities. Charity help is not counted in the public charge test — only government cash assistance counts under the current rule.

Member Diaper Banks — National Diaper Bank Network

programs.name: Emergency Relief Grants
programs.org: CERF+ (Craft Emergency Relief Fund)
programs.gradeRationale: Rolling applications year-round, one clear online form (English or Spanish), a flat $3,000, and four decades of steady funding since 1985. Currently slowed a bit by high application volume, and it only serves craft artists with a real recent emergency.
programs.oneLiner: $3,000 for craft artists hit by disaster or illness
programs.whatIs: CERF+ gives $3,000 grants to craft artists whose life or work was knocked sideways by a recent emergency — a fire, flood, storm, theft, accident, injury, or major illness. You can spend the money on your recovery however you need, you never have to report back, and the grant is not taxable income. It has helped craft artists since 1985.
programs.whoArrives: A potter whose studio flooded, a jeweler who broke a hand and can't work, a quiltmaker who lost tools and materials in a house fire. A friend or family member can apply for the artist with their permission.
eligibility: Individual craft artist making handmade 3-D objects (clay, glass, fiber, wood, metal, leather, beadwork, and more)
A public-facing craft practice — recent shows, sales, press, or an active online presence
Age 18 or older
Lived and worked in the U.S. or a U.S. Territory for the past 2 years
A recent, seriously disruptive emergency or disaster (routine medical care and slow business don't count)
Limit: 1 grant per year, 4 per lifetime
programs.openTo: No citizenship or SSN requirement in the published rules — you need 2 years living and working in the U.S. or a U.S. Territory, and every application must pass an identity check run through a third-party service (ID Pal)
programs.cost: $0 to apply
howToApply: Go to cerfplus.org/grants/emergency-relief (application also available in Spanish)
Complete the online application and describe your emergency
Upload supporting documents — photos, bills, or repair estimates
Finish the ID Pal identity verification step (your application isn't complete without it)
Email programs@cerfplus.org or call (802) 229-2306 with questions
docsNeeded: Proof of the emergency (photos, medical bills, insurance or repair estimates)
Examples of your recent, public-facing craft practice
Identity documents for the ID Pal verification step

claimChecks.claim: Emergency grant money counts as taxable income.
claimChecks.explanation: CERF+ says its Emergency Relief Grants are non-taxable grants/gifts. The IRS does not require CERF+ to issue a Form 1099, and you don't have to report how you spent the money.

claimChecks.claim: CERF+ only helps after big natural disasters.
claimChecks.explanation: Personal emergencies count too — theft, accidents, injuries, and major illness all qualify alongside fires and floods. Routine medical care, equipment failure, and slow sales don't.

programs.name: Emergency Financial Assistance Grants
programs.org: Musicians Foundation
programs.gradeRationale: The application is always open, help typically arrives in as little as one to two weeks, and the fund has operated since 1914. The catch is a narrow door: you need 5+ years of U.S. tax returns showing music work.
programs.oneLiner: Pays a struggling musician's medical or housing bill fast
programs.whatIs: The Musicians Foundation pays bills for professional musicians in a time of need — grants typically run $500 to $3,000. The check goes straight to whoever you owe: the hospital, doctor, landlord, or utility company. Any genre counts, and the fund has been doing this since 1914.
programs.whoArrives: A gigging musician sidelined by surgery who can't cover rent, or a longtime music teacher facing a hospital bill after their hours got cut.
eligibility: Professional music performer, composer/arranger, or music educator
5+ years working as a professional musician in the U.S.
Currently live in the U.S.
Filed taxes as a musician for 5+ years and can provide a recent tax return
In a specific time of need — e.g. medical bills, rent or mortgage, or utilities you can't cover
programs.openTo: No citizenship rule is published — you must live in the U.S. and show tax returns from 5+ years of music work; the rules don't mention an SSN, and U.S. tax returns can also be filed with an ITIN
programs.cost: $0 to apply
howToApply: Start the online application at musiciansfoundation.org/apply — it's always open
Complete Part 1 to confirm you're eligible
If invited, submit Part 2 documents: a recent tax return and the bills you need paid
Call 212-239-9137 or email info@musiciansfoundation.org if you get stuck
docsNeeded: A recent tax return showing your work as a musician
Copies of the bills you need paid (hospital, landlord, utility, etc.)
Proof of your professional music career (5+ years)

claimChecks.claim: You have to belong to the musicians' union to get help.
claimChecks.explanation: Union membership is not part of the published requirements. Any professional musician — performer, composer/arranger, or educator, in any genre — can apply if they meet the 5-year career, tax, and residency rules.

claimChecks.claim: The grant is cash you can spend on anything.
claimChecks.explanation: Checks are made out directly to the biller — the doctor, hospital, landlord, or utility provider — and mailed to the approved applicant. It clears your bill rather than putting cash in your pocket.

programs.name: Emergency Grants
programs.org: Foundation for Contemporary Arts
programs.gradeRationale: Year-round, national, and decided monthly — genuinely fast for the arts world. But only about 15-20 of the roughly 100 monthly applicants get funded, and it covers project costs only, for experimental work.
programs.oneLiner: Quick $500 to $3,000 when a confirmed show hits surprise costs
programs.whatIs: FCA gives $500 to $3,000 (average $2,200) to visual artists, performing artists, and poets who suddenly get a chance to show their work, or whose almost-finished project hits unexpected costs. It runs all year and decides every month. It is for project expenses tied to a confirmed public show — not rent or medical bills.
programs.whoArrives: An artist whose exhibition opens in six weeks when a shipping or equipment cost appears out of nowhere, or a performer who just got invited to present work with no time to fundraise.
eligibility: Visual or performing artists and poets making innovative, experimental work
Living in the U.S. or a U.S. Territory with a U.S. tax ID
A committed show, performance, or reading with specific dates
Not enrolled in any degree program
No FCA Emergency Grant or Creative Research Grant in the past 3 years
programs.openTo: No citizenship requirement — you must live in the U.S. and have a U.S. Tax ID Number, and FCA's guidelines say an SSN, ITIN, EIN, or other tax ID all work
programs.cost: $0 to apply
howToApply: Read the guidelines and FAQs at foundationforcontemporaryarts.org
Watch FCA's recorded information session (recommended, not required)
Apply online 8-10 weeks before your show or performance date — no earlier than 10 weeks out
Request any amount from $500 to $3,000 with a simple budget
docsNeeded: Work samples
Project description with confirmed presentation dates
Budget for the amount you're requesting
U.S. tax ID (SSN, ITIN, or EIN)

claimChecks.claim: An arts emergency grant can cover my rent or medical bills.
claimChecks.explanation: Not this one — FCA Emergency Grants exclude non-project life expenses such as food, rent, medical bills, and childcare. Other funds on this list (CERF+, Rauschenberg) do cover life emergencies.

claimChecks.claim: You have to be a U.S. citizen to get an art grant.
claimChecks.explanation: FCA requires that you live in the U.S. and have a U.S. tax ID — its guidelines list SSN, EIN, ITIN, or other. Citizenship is not required.

programs.name: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants
programs.org: Robert Rauschenberg Foundation, administered by NYFA
programs.gradeRationale: Nationwide, built for ordinary working artists, and it covers dental and mental health care, not just medical. But cycles run every couple of months, answers take about two months, and NYFA is upfront that need far outpaces the money — after review, even strong applications go into a lottery.
programs.oneLiner: Up to $5,000 toward an artist's medical or dental bills
programs.whatIs: One-time grants of up to $5,000 for a recent unexpected medical, dental, or mental health emergency. It's for visual artists, film/video and digital artists, and choreographers. Application cycles open every couple of months, and grants are usually sized to your actual eligible bills, up to the cap. Funds are limited: after staff and panel review, the top-scoring application is funded and the rest of the top tier goes into a lottery.
programs.whoArrives: An uninsured painter staring at an ER bill, or a choreographer who needs an emergency root canal and has no way to pay for it.
eligibility: Age 21 or older
Artist making your own work in visual arts, film/video/electronic/digital arts, or choreography
Live in the U.S., D.C., a Tribal Nation, or a U.S. Territory
Income of $80,000 or less ($160,000 for joint filers), averaged over your last two federal tax returns
Public artistic activity at least once a year over the last 5 years; no Rauschenberg emergency grant in the last 5 years
Not enrolled in any degree-seeking program
programs.openTo: No citizenship requirement in the eligibility rules — you must live in the U.S. and have filed federal tax returns, which ITIN filers (no SSN) can do; applications must be in English but a proxy or translator can help you complete one
programs.cost: $0 to apply
howToApply: Check the current cycle dates at nyfa.org (search 'Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants')
Gather your medical or dental bills and treatment records — estimates are OK if you don't have bills yet
Apply online via Submittable during the open window — windows last about a month
Email emergencyfunds@nyfa.org with any questions
docsNeeded: Medical or dental bills, treatment records, or your own cost estimate
Your adjusted gross income from your last two federal tax returns
Proof of your artistic activity (shows, screenings, or performances — no work samples needed)

claimChecks.claim: No grant will ever help an artist pay a dental bill.
claimChecks.explanation: This fund explicitly covers dental and mental health emergencies as well as medical ones, with one-time grants up to $5,000.

claimChecks.claim: You have to be a famous artist to qualify.
claimChecks.explanation: The opposite — your income must be under $80,000 ($160,000 joint), and what counts is public artistic activity roughly once a year for five years, not fame. Portfolios aren't even reviewed.

programs.name: U.S. Writers Aid Initiative (Writers Emergency Fund)
programs.org: PEN America
programs.gradeRationale: Real and national with light paperwork, and no PEN membership needed. But grants are modest (roughly $500 to $3,500 depending on the year's funding), applications only open in three short windows per year, and PEN says the fund is limited — not every application can be supported.
programs.oneLiner: One-time cash for writers in a financial emergency
programs.whatIs: PEN America gives one-time grants to professional writers facing a sudden, short-term financial emergency. PEN doesn't publish a fixed amount — pandemic-era grants ran $500 to $1,000, and the relaunched program has offered up to $3,500 depending on need. It covers fiction and nonfiction authors, poets, playwrights, translators, and journalists. Applications open in three short windows a year, and decisions come by the end of that cycle's month.
programs.whoArrives: A freelance journalist whose income collapsed after an illness, or a poet a month behind on rent after an unexpected expense.
eligibility: Professional writer: published books (self-published-only doesn't count), literary journal publications, a professionally produced play, or staff/freelance journalism
Based in the United States
An acute, short-term financial emergency this one-time grant would meaningfully help
Not currently enrolled in a degree-granting program
Limit: 2 Writers Aid grants per lifetime
programs.openTo: Must be based in the U.S.; no citizenship or SSN requirement stated in the eligibility rules
programs.cost: $0 to apply
howToApply: Go to pen.org/us-writers-aid-initiative
Check the next cycle's dates (2026: March 15-31, June 1-15, and September 15-October 5)
Submit the online application describing your writing career and the emergency
If you're a finalist, send the supporting documents PEN requests before funds go out
Email writersfund@pen.org with questions
docsNeeded: Proof of your writing career (publications, productions, or contracts)
A short description of the emergency and what you need
Supporting documentation if you're selected as a finalist

claimChecks.claim: You have to be a PEN America member to get help.
claimChecks.explanation: Membership is not required to apply or receive a grant. Recipients actually get a free one-year PEN America membership with their award.

claimChecks.claim: Emergency writer funds are only for famous authors.
claimChecks.explanation: It's need-based. Freelance journalists, translators, poets, and playwrights qualify with ordinary professional credits like journal publications or produced work.

programs.name: MacDowell Fellowship (Artist Residency)
programs.org: MacDowell
programs.gradeRationale: The residency itself is a dream — free, with travel money and stipends — and it's open worldwide at every career stage. But it's very competitive (about 300 fellowships a year from a much larger field), there are only two deadlines annually, and help arrives many months after you apply.
programs.oneLiner: Free room, meals, and studio for weeks of art-making
programs.whatIs: MacDowell gives artists a private studio, a room, and three prepared meals a day for up to 8 weeks in Peterborough, New Hampshire — completely free. Travel to and from is covered by grants, and need-based stipends of up to $1,500 can help with the rent, utilities, childcare, and lost income you'd face back home while you're away. More than 300 artists receive fellowships each year across seven art forms.
programs.whoArrives: Artists who can't finish a project between shifts and side gigs, and parents or working artists who assume residencies are only for people who can afford unpaid time away.
eligibility: Artists in architecture, film/video, interdisciplinary arts, literature, music composition, theatre, or visual arts
Any career stage — emerging artists are welcome
Artists from any country (conversational English recommended; applications accepted in English and Spanish)
Not a degree-seeking student during your program (doctoral candidates who finished coursework can apply)
The sole criterion for acceptance is artistic excellence
programs.openTo: Open to artists from any country — no U.S. immigration status or SSN needed to apply
programs.cost: $30 application fee (fee waiver available for financial hardship); the residency itself is free
howToApply: Read the guidelines at macdowell.org/apply
Pick a deadline: around September 10 for the following spring/summer, around February 10 for fall/winter
Submit work samples from the past four years and a project description through the online portal
Request a fee waiver inside the application before submitting if $30 is a hardship
Ask about travel grants and need-based stipends once admitted
docsNeeded: Work samples in your discipline (completed within the past four years)
Project description
$30 fee or an approved fee waiver

claimChecks.claim: Artist residencies always cost money.
claimChecks.explanation: MacDowell charges no residency fees and offers travel grants. Need-based stipends of up to $1,500 can cover rent, utilities, childcare, and lost income while you're there. (Some other residencies do charge — always check.)

claimChecks.claim: You need an MFA or a big exhibition record to get in.
claimChecks.explanation: MacDowell accepts artists at all career stages from all backgrounds, and says the sole criterion for acceptance is artistic excellence — judged largely from your work samples, not your resume.

programs.name: Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grant
programs.org: The Pollock-Krasner Foundation
programs.gradeRationale: Generous (up to $50,000, most grants $5,000-$30,000), worldwide, and you can apply any day of the year with no fee. But review takes 9 to 12 months and you need an active professional exhibition record — this is a lifeline for working artists in a hard year, not a fast fix.
programs.oneLiner: Large grants for painters and sculptors, apply any time
programs.whatIs: The Pollock-Krasner Foundation gives grants of up to $50,000 — most run between $5,000 and $30,000 — to painters, sculptors, and artists who work on paper (including printmakers). The money can cover both professional and personal expenses — studio rent, materials, living costs — and the amount is sized to your actual situation. You can apply year-round, but expect to wait 9 to 12 months for a decision.
programs.whoArrives: A mid-career painter in a lean year between sales, or a sculptor whose savings were wiped out by an emergency and needs breathing room to keep working.
eligibility: Painters, sculptors, and artists working on paper (including printmakers)
Actively exhibiting current work in professional venues like galleries and museums
Demonstrable financial need — professional, personal, or both
Artists worldwide (grantees in 80 countries so far)
Not eligible: students, commercial artists, graphic designers, video/performance artists, filmmakers, and craft artists; photographers are considered by nomination only
programs.openTo: Open to artists worldwide — no U.S. immigration status or SSN needed; applicants in US-sanctioned countries must contact the foundation before applying
programs.cost: $0 to apply
howToApply: Go to pkf.org/apply and read the guidelines
Write a cover letter stating why you need funding and how much
Prepare your CV with exhibition history, a one-page artist statement, and 10 digital images of work from the past 10 years with an image list
Submit through the foundation's online application system (drafts left untouched for 120 days are deleted)
Expect an answer in 9 to 12 months
docsNeeded: Cover letter with the amount you need and why
Resume/CV with exhibition history
One-page artist statement
10 high-quality digital images of recent work plus an image identification list

claimChecks.claim: There's an annual deadline, and if you miss it you wait a year.
claimChecks.explanation: There are no deadlines at all. Applications are accepted year-round and reviewed on a rolling basis — you can apply today.

claimChecks.claim: Big art foundation grants are only for U.S. artists.
claimChecks.explanation: Pollock-Krasner funds artists globally — its grantees span 80 countries and over $95 million awarded since 1985. Only artists in US-sanctioned countries need to contact the foundation first.

programs.name: SCORE Business Mentoring
programs.org: SCORE (nonprofit resource partner of the U.S. Small Business Administration)
programs.gradeRationale: Free in all 50 states, no eligibility screening, and SCORE says a mentor typically responds to your request within about 48 hours. Federally supported since 1964, so it's reliably funded and not going anywhere.
programs.oneLiner: Free expert business mentor, matched within days
programs.whatIs: SCORE pairs you with a volunteer business mentor for free — a retired executive or business owner who has done what you're trying to do. You can meet by video, phone, email, or in person, and keep meeting as long as you want. They also run free webinars and workshops on everything from pricing to marketing.
programs.whoArrives: People with a business idea and no clue where to start, or owners hitting a wall — slow sales, confusing taxes, a loan application they don't understand. Many arrive after being quoted thousands by paid 'business coaches.'
eligibility: Anyone thinking about starting a business — no business required yet
Existing small business owners at any stage
All 50 states and U.S. territories, in person or remote
No income, credit, or paperwork requirements
programs.openTo: Open to everyone — no immigration status, SSN, or citizenship requirement to get a mentor.
programs.cost: $0 — always free. Anyone charging you for 'SCORE mentoring' or SBA help is running a scam.
howToApply: Go to score.org and click 'Find a Mentor'
Enter your ZIP code to see mentors near you, or choose remote mentoring
Pick a mentor by industry experience, or take the first available match
A mentor typically reaches out within about 48 hours
Keep meeting as often as you like — it stays free forever
docsNeeded: None — just sign up online with your name and email

claimChecks.claim: Free business help is really a sales pitch — they'll charge you later.
claimChecks.explanation: SCORE is a nonprofit funded through the SBA, and its mentors are unpaid volunteers. Mentoring is free for as long as you use it, with nothing to buy.

claimChecks.claim: You need to already own a business to get a mentor.
claimChecks.explanation: SCORE explicitly serves people at the idea stage. Many mentees show up with nothing but a notion and leave with a business plan.

programs.name: Small Business Development Centers (SBDC)
programs.org: America's SBDC network, funded by the SBA and hosted by universities and state agencies
programs.gradeRationale: Nearly 1,000 centers nationwide with free, professional one-on-one consulting — everyone who asks gets served. Graded A instead of S only because you usually book an appointment and wait a few days to a couple of weeks depending on the center.
programs.oneLiner: Free professional business consulting at nearly 1,000 centers
programs.whatIs: SBDCs give you a professional business advisor for free — not just a chat, but real help building a business plan, reading your financials, and packaging a loan application lenders will take seriously. There are almost 1,000 centers, usually hosted at local colleges. Training workshops are free or low-cost.
programs.whoArrives: Founders who got turned down for a loan and don't know why, people drowning in licensing and tax questions, and owners who need someone to look at their numbers before things get worse.
eligibility: Anyone planning to start a small business ('pre-venture' is welcome)
Existing small business owners who want to grow or fix problems
Every state has centers — find yours by ZIP code
No income or credit requirements for advising
programs.openTo: Advising is open to everyone — no immigration-status or SSN requirement to sit down with an advisor. (Loan programs they help you apply to can have their own rules, including new SBA citizenship rules.)
programs.cost: $0 for one-on-one advising; some training workshops charge small fees, which each center posts up front.
howToApply: Visit americassbdc.org and click 'Find Your SBDC', or search sba.gov/sbdc by ZIP code
Call or complete your local center's short intake form
Book a free advising session (many offer video appointments)
Bring whatever you have — an idea, a shoebox of receipts, or a declined loan application
Return as often as you need; advising stays free
docsNeeded: None to start — bring a business plan or financials later if you have them

claimChecks.claim: Government business help is only for established companies, not tiny startups.
claimChecks.explanation: SBDCs explicitly serve 'pre-venture entrepreneurs' — people who haven't opened yet. Startup planning is one of their core services.

claimChecks.claim: The advisor will want a cut of my business or push me toward a specific bank.
claimChecks.explanation: SBDC advisors are paid through federal and state funding. They take no equity, no commissions, and no referral fees.

programs.name: SBA Microloan Program
programs.org: U.S. Small Business Administration, through nonprofit intermediary lenders
programs.gradeRationale: Available nationwide through community nonprofits that coach you through the process, but it's still a real loan with paperwork, collateral, and a decision that takes weeks. A harsh April 2026 rule change also cut off everyone who isn't a U.S. citizen or national.
programs.oneLiner: Business loans up to $50,000 through friendly local nonprofits
programs.whatIs: The SBA gives money to nonprofit community lenders, who lend it out in amounts up to $50,000 — the average loan is about $13,000. Rates generally run 8% to 13%, with up to 7 years to repay. Unlike a bank, these lenders also coach you before, during, and after the loan.
programs.whoArrives: New and young businesses that banks won't touch — food vendors, cleaners, barbers, childcare providers — who need equipment, inventory, or working capital, not a quarter-million-dollar loan.
eligibility: For-profit small businesses, including startups, plus some nonprofit childcare centers
As of April 1, 2026, every owner must be a U.S. citizen or U.S. national
Each nonprofit lender sets its own credit rules — most are flexible
Usually requires some collateral and a personal guarantee
Funds can't pay off existing debt or buy real estate
programs.openTo: As of April 1, 2026, 100% of a business's owners must be U.S. citizens or U.S. nationals — green card holders, DACA recipients, and visa holders no longer qualify under SBA's updated rules.
programs.cost: $0 to apply with most intermediaries; some lenders charge packaging or closing fees, so ask each one up front. Loans generally carry 8-13% interest.
howToApply: Open sba.gov/funding-programs/loans/microloans and find the list of approved intermediaries
Call the intermediary serving your area and ask about their requirements
Prepare a simple business plan and basic financials — many intermediaries help you for free
Submit the application through the intermediary; they make the credit decision, not the SBA
Expect an answer within a few weeks
docsNeeded: Business plan
Personal and business tax returns
Bank statements
Government photo ID and proof of citizenship or U.S. national status
List of collateral

claimChecks.claim: The SBA lends money directly to business owners.
claimChecks.explanation: For microloans (and most SBA loans), nonprofit intermediaries or banks lend the money — the SBA backs or funds them. The main exception is disaster loans, which the SBA does make directly.

claimChecks.claim: Green card holders qualify for SBA loans.
claimChecks.explanation: This was true for years, but SBA rule changes effective March-April 2026 require 100% of business owners to be U.S. citizens or U.S. nationals. Lawful permanent residents are now excluded.

claimChecks.claim: You need bank-level credit and collateral to get a microloan.
claimChecks.explanation: Intermediaries are far more flexible than banks and often work with thin or damaged credit, but most still ask for some collateral and a personal guarantee.

programs.name: Kiva U.S. Crowdfunded Loans
programs.org: Kiva (501(c)(3) nonprofit)
programs.gradeRationale: Anyone with a business purpose can apply — no credit score, no collateral, truly 0% interest — but you have to recruit friends and family to lend first, and the whole pipeline from application to cash typically takes one to two months. Real, but it takes hustle.
programs.oneLiner: Crowdfunded business loans up to $15,000 at 0% interest
programs.whatIs: Kiva lets you borrow $1,000 to $15,000 for your business at 0% interest with zero fees — the money comes from regular people around the world who chip in $25 at a time. There's no credit score requirement; Kiva judges 'character over credit.' You repay monthly over 12 to 36 months.
programs.whoArrives: Founders with no credit history, immigrant entrepreneurs, and side-hustlers going full time — people who need a few thousand dollars and have a community that believes in them, but no bank that does.
eligibility: 18 or older, living and running the business in the U.S. (not Nevada or North Dakota)
Loan must be for business purposes — not refinancing debt
Not currently in bankruptcy or foreclosure, and no financial or violent convictions in 5 years
Must have a PayPal account to receive and repay the loan
Willing to recruit 5-40 friends/family to lend during a private period
programs.openTo: Kiva itself has no citizenship or immigration-status requirement, doesn't ask for an SSN, and runs no credit check. You do need a PayPal account, and PayPal's identity verification typically asks for an SSN or ITIN.
programs.cost: $0 — 0% interest, no fees, ever. Anyone charging a fee to 'get you a Kiva loan' is a scammer; the real application is free at kiva.org.
howToApply: Apply at kiva.org/borrow — the application takes 30-60 minutes
Wait about 10-15 business days for Kiva's approval decision
Recruit 5-40 people you know to lend $25+ during a private period of about 10-15 days
Go public to Kiva's worldwide lenders for roughly 20-30 more days
Receive funds through PayPal and repay monthly over 12-36 months
docsNeeded: PayPal account
A photo and your business story for the loan page
Basic business and financial details (no credit report pulled)

claimChecks.claim: A 0% interest loan always has hidden fees somewhere.
claimChecks.explanation: Kiva charges borrowers no interest and no fees of any kind — the program is funded by donors and lenders who accept zero return. The cost of borrowing is genuinely $0.

claimChecks.claim: You can't get a business loan without a credit score.
claimChecks.explanation: Kiva has no minimum credit score and doesn't pull traditional credit. Approval is based on your story and your community vouching for you with real loans.

programs.name: Grameen America Microloan Program
programs.org: Grameen America (nonprofit microlender)
programs.gradeRationale: If you qualify, acceptance odds are excellent: no credit score, no collateral, no bank account needed, and first loans flow within a few weeks of joining. Graded B, not A, because it's for low-income women only, you must live near a branch (roughly two dozen cities), form a five-woman group, and commit to weekly meetings.
programs.oneLiner: Small startup loans for women, no credit score needed
programs.whatIs: Grameen America gives first-time loans of $500 to $2,500 to low-income women entrepreneurs — no credit history, no collateral, no bank account required. You join a group of five women, complete a week of free financial training, and repay weekly over six months. Loans grow with each cycle, and payments are reported to Experian and Equifax so you build a credit score.
programs.whoArrives: Women selling food, doing hair, cleaning houses, or running market stalls — often immigrant moms shut out of banks entirely — who need a small, fair loan and a credit history, not a payday lender.
eligibility: Women 18+ with low income (program targets women below the federal poverty line)
Live in or near a Grameen America branch city (20+ U.S. cities, including NYC, LA, Houston, Miami, Atlanta)
Willing to form or join a five-woman group and attend short weekly meetings
No credit score, collateral, guarantor, or bank account required
programs.openTo: No credit score, bank account, or collateral required, and no SSN requirement is listed. Branches serve largely immigrant communities — your local branch will tell you exactly what ID works.
programs.cost: $0 to join and $0 in fees; loans carry 15-18% interest on a declining balance with no origination, late, or monthly fees.
howToApply: Check grameenamerica.org for a branch in your city
Submit the loan inquiry form at grameenamerica.org/request-a-loan
Form a group of five with women you trust, or join an existing group
Complete one week of free financial training
Receive your first loan ($500-$2,500) and attend 30-minute weekly meetings
docsNeeded: Photo ID (ask your branch what counts)
No credit report, bank statements, or collateral documents

claimChecks.claim: In group lending, you're on the hook if a woman in your group doesn't pay.
claimChecks.explanation: Grameen America's FAQ is explicit: members are not financially responsible for other members' loans. The group exists for peer support, not as a co-signer arrangement.

claimChecks.claim: You need a bank account and a credit score to start building credit.
claimChecks.explanation: Grameen requires neither, and it reports your repayments to Experian and Equifax — many members build their first-ever credit score this way.

programs.name: CDFI Small Business Loans (find one near you)
programs.org: Community Development Financial Institutions, certified by the U.S. Treasury's CDFI Fund
programs.gradeRationale: There are certified CDFIs in every state and they exist specifically to lend to people banks reject, with flexible underwriting and free coaching. Graded B because each lender has its own products, paperwork, and timelines — you have to call around, and it's still a loan decision.
programs.oneLiner: Mission-driven local lenders who say yes when banks say no
programs.whatIs: CDFIs are banks, credit unions, and loan funds certified by the U.S. Treasury to serve communities that mainstream banks skip. They make small business loans with flexible credit rules, fair rates, and usually free business coaching on the side. Most people have never heard of them — and there's almost certainly one serving your area.
programs.whoArrives: Business owners who got a 'no' from a bank — thin credit, an ITIN instead of an SSN, a business in a neighborhood lenders redline — and assume that 'no' was final. It usually isn't.
eligibility: Small business owners and startups in the lender's service area
Each CDFI sets its own credit and documentation rules — most are flexible by design
Many focus on low-income, rural, Native, immigrant, or minority communities
Both existing businesses and startups, depending on the lender
programs.openTo: Varies by lender — many CDFIs accept ITINs and lend regardless of immigration status, but each sets its own policy. Ask 'do you lend to ITIN holders?' before you apply.
programs.cost: $0 to ask; loan rates and fees vary by lender — get them in writing before you sign. Typically far cheaper than online lenders or merchant cash advances.
howToApply: Open cdfifund.gov and use the searchable certified CDFI list or awards database to find lenders in your state
Filter to loan funds and credit unions near you
Call 2-3 of them and ask: loan sizes, ITIN policy, credit requirements, and timelines
Ask about free business coaching — most CDFIs offer it alongside loans
Apply with the lender that fits your situation best
docsNeeded: Varies by lender — typically photo ID (SSN or ITIN at many), bank statements or tax returns, and a simple business plan

claimChecks.claim: If the bank turned me down, nobody will lend to me.
claimChecks.explanation: CDFIs exist precisely to lend to creditworthy people banks reject. Flexible underwriting for underserved borrowers is their federally certified mission, not an exception.

claimChecks.claim: These community lenders are just unregulated payday-style lenders.
claimChecks.explanation: CDFIs are certified and monitored by the U.S. Treasury Department's CDFI Fund, and many are regulated banks or credit unions. Their rates are typically far below payday or merchant-cash-advance products.

programs.name: Amber Grant for Women
programs.org: WomensNet
programs.gradeRationale: Real money, a genuinely short application, and it's been running since 1998 — but only three $10,000 winners a month against thousands of applicants makes it lottery-ish odds, and there's a $15 fee per application. Apply, but don't plan around it.
programs.oneLiner: Monthly $10,000 grants for women-owned businesses
programs.whatIs: WomensNet awards three $10,000 Amber Grants every month to women-owned businesses, chosen by an advisory board that reads your story and plans. Monthly winners are automatically in the running for three $50,000 year-end grants. The application is short — no long forms — and one application enters you into every grant you qualify for.
programs.whoArrives: Women running or launching small businesses who need a cash cushion that isn't debt — and women burned out on 'grant lists' full of dead links and scams looking for one that actually pays out.
eligibility: Women 18 or older
Business at least 50% women-owned
Based in the United States or Canada
Revenue-generating nonprofits qualify if women hold 50%+ of top leadership, including the board president or CEO
programs.openTo: Open to women 18+ with a U.S. or Canadian business; no SSN or immigration-status requirement is stated in the rules.
programs.cost: $15 non-refundable application fee (WomensNet says fee waivers are available on request). Be careful: this is a rare legit exception; 'government grants' that ask for fees are always scams.
howToApply: Read the rules at ambergrantsforwomen.com/get-an-amber-grant
Complete the short online application — tell your story and how you'd use $10,000
Pay the $15 fee (or ask for a waiver) and submit by the last day of the month (11:59 pm ET)
Watch for winner announcements by the 21st of the following month
Reapply after three months if something significant about your business changes
docsNeeded: None beyond the online form — no tax returns or financial statements required to apply

claimChecks.claim: A real grant never charges an application fee.
claimChecks.explanation: As a rule of thumb it's a great scam detector — no government grant ever charges a fee. The Amber Grant is a rare legitimate private exception with a disclosed $15 fee it has charged openly for years, and it offers waivers on request.

claimChecks.claim: You have to apply separately for each WomensNet grant.
claimChecks.explanation: One application enters you into all the grants you're eligible for, including the monthly $10,000 awards and the $50,000 year-end grants.
